title: Bootstrap CLI standalone socket readiness is nondeterministic in Nix closure
description:
Cacophony's reviewed combined lock preflight builds exact full-green upstream Pi Daemon source `73d88e7c8330a2acd9a9cb6933008c6f921c3d3e`, but the local Nix closure failed one deterministic-gate test:

- file: `test/bootstrap-cli.test.mjs:34`
- test: `serve bootstraps an empty standalone instance...`
- failure: `ECONNREFUSED` connecting to the expected `run/pi-daemon.sock`
- derivation: `/nix/store/69rq...-pi-daemon-0.3.0.drv`
- result: 589 tests, 585 pass, 3 skipped, 1 fail
- upstream provider checks for the same source are 12/12 green across Linux/Darwin/Node/Nix/contracts

Update-helper preserved the exact two-input Cacophony flake.lock diff uncommitted and refused retry/bypass, so this is source/harness nondeterminism exposed by the downstream closure rather than a pin mutation.

Required fix:

- reproduce the bootstrap socket race in a hermetic Nix build/check environment without relying on ambient service state
- make the test wait on bounded semantic readiness or explicit child exit, not a fixed timing gap or socket-path existence alone
- preserve exact standalone instance paths and fail closed if the daemon exits, binds the wrong socket, or never answers
- emit bounded child stderr/exit/socket diagnostics on failure without secrets or unbounded logs
- add a regression that delays listener readiness and proves no ECONNREFUSED, plus a dead-child case that fails promptly
- retain process cleanup and zero residual services
- prove repeated Nix closure builds and upstream Node/Nix lanes are green; do not paper over with blind retry, ignored test, or extended unbounded sleep
- return exact source/main/CI receipt so Cacophony can regenerate the preserved combined Pi/Cara lock diff

No existing Pi Daemon bead matched the test name, file, ECONNREFUSED socket, or bootstrap-socket wording across all statuses.

title: [broken-on-main] bootstrap CLI SIGTERM race returns signal exit
description:
`nix flake check` and a direct Nix package-check retry both fail `serve bootstraps an empty standalone instance before constructing the Pi factory` at `test/bootstrap-cli.test.mjs:95`: the child exit event reports `exitCode === null` after SIGTERM rather than graceful code 0. The exact isolated Node test and full local `npm test` pass. Root cause: `serve` publishes/listens on the owner socket before `waitForSignal()` installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers, so a client that handshakes immediately can signal during that startup window and receive the platform default termination. Add an early bounded signal latch that is installed before listeners become visible, drains through the existing whole-deadline shutdown once startup ownership exists, and is disposed on startup failure/injected shutdown. Include deterministic race coverage. Observed while validating bd-5c06cd; pre-existing on main.

title: Run the cheap Nix checks as a fast lane ahead of the full flake check
description:
The `nix` CI job runs `nix flake check --print-build-logs` as one opaque step
with a 25-minute timeout. Every check therefore shares the fate, and the
schedule, of the most expensive one: the full package build plus `npm test`.

That matters for the cheap checks specifically. bd-acf2d3 added
`checks.<system>.npm-deps-hash`, which only fetches the npm dependency cache and
reports the exact replacement hash on a stale pin. It answers in about a minute
standalone, but inside `nix flake check` its answer arrives interleaved with a
build that can run for twenty more. The same applies to
`home-manager-module`, which is also cheap.

Suggested shape: run the cheap checks as an explicit earlier step, for example
`nix build .#checks.<system>.npm-deps-hash .#checks.<system>.home-manager-module`
with a short timeout, before the full `nix flake check`. The full check stays
authoritative and unchanged; the fast lane just moves a class of clear, quickly
knowable failures to the front. Worth measuring the real standalone times first
rather than assuming the split pays for itself.

Observed while landing bd-acf2d3.

Filed via reflect-session mixin from bd-acf2d3 session.
creator: sonance:pi-daemon:sonance-pi-daemon-pidm-pico-on-demand-dev-test-son

title: Bound protocol event and response serialization before allocation
description: Resource-bound finding from bd-62e2c5. Model message events are not journal-record bounded, and mapped Pi event payloads can contain full messages, tool results, or provider error data. Therefore the advertised outbound bound controls only queued bytes after an unbounded JSON serialization and allocation. Define per-event and per-response payload limits, use bounded serialization or deliberate truncation and typed overflow behavior, prevent non-serializable SDK payloads from disrupting session delivery, and add adversarial tests proving a large event cannot grow process memory or affect other sessions.

title: Fix closure-cache workflow invalid job-level runner context
description:
True-main workflow commit e4f0aec (bd-9de467) produced hosted run 30761047479 with conclusion=failure and zero jobs/check-runs; GitHub named it by path instead of declared workflow name, proving pre-job validation failure. Pinned actionlint against `.github/workflows/closure-cache.yml` gives the exact error:

  line 49: context "runner" is not allowed here
  XDG_CONFIG_HOME: ${{ runner.temp }}/pi-daemon-closure-${{ matrix.system }}-xdg

At job-level `env`, available contexts exclude `runner`; therefore all four target jobs are rejected before Attic/devshell/build/version/push steps. Move XDG_CONFIG_HOME initialization into an early shell step that writes `$RUNNER_TEMP/...` to `$GITHUB_ENV` (the original aarch64 workflow used this valid pattern), or another step-scoped equivalent. Keep `matrix.system` target separation and isolated per-target config. Add pinned actionlint or an equivalent negative source contract proving runner context cannot return at job scope. Run actionlint plus focused CI boundary tests, land, and manually dispatch/rerun the closure publisher to collect per-target build/version/push/signed-substitution receipts.

Reproduction command used repository-pinned nixpkgs:
  nix shell github:NixOS/nixpkgs/d407951447dcd00442e97087bf374aad70c04cea#actionlint -c actionlint .github/workflows/closure-cache.yml

No target build or cache push ran in failed run 30761047479.

title: [broken-on-main] Node CI lane fails five TLS tests: test fixture requires openssl on PATH
description:
Both Node jobs of the CI workflow (22.19.0 and 24) fail five tests on main, and have since at least d93900d, independently of any change under review:

    Error: spawn openssl ENOENT
    test/dashboard-dedicated-cli.test.mjs:62  dedicated web CLI authenticates remotely and serves only browser credentials
    test/dashboard-identity-config.test.mjs:79  provider documents and credential sources fail closed
    test/dashboard-server.test.mjs:314  loads bounded owner-controlled TLS file and descriptor sources
    (+2 further TLS cases: native HTTPS SNI/HSTS/downgrade, file-backed TLS rotation)

Cause: `test/tls-fixture.mjs` shells out to `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 ...` to mint the dashboard TLS pair. The Node jobs run under `actions/setup-node` with no Nix shell, so `openssl` is not on PATH. Every developer machine has it, which is why a local `npm test` is green and this never surfaces outside CI. `nix flake check` on Linux passes, so only the Node lane is affected.

This is the same class as a browser-launching case sitting in the standard gate directory: a test whose environmental assumptions hold locally and in one CI lane but not in the lane that actually runs it.

Do not fix it by skipping when openssl is absent. These are the TLS and credential fail-closed cases; silently skipping them on CI is worse than the current honest red, because the gate would go green while the security coverage quietly disappears.

Candidate fixes, in rough order of preference:
1. An `OPENSSL_BIN` override in `test/tls-fixture.mjs` plus a CI step that resolves openssl from the flake's own nixpkgs onto PATH. Keeps the Node version matrix intact, keeps coverage, no new dependency.
2. Run the Node lane's `npm test` inside a Nix shell that provides openssl. Simpler, but it replaces the matrix's Node with the flake's Node, which defeats the point of testing 22.19.0 and 24.
3. Generate the pair in pure Node. `node:crypto` parses X.509 but cannot issue, so this means hand-rolled ASN.1 or a new dev dependency; both are heavier than the problem.

Whoever takes it should also check the failing `Nix (macOS)` job, which is red in the same runs with a signature I have not read.

title: Widen the reported-figure rule to any quoted measurement, and give it a mechanism
description:
Scope correction to the rule landed in cfda630, from the agent whose instance it
fails to cover.

As written it says "every figure in a verification report comes from the run
being reported". Their instance was not in a report: it was a load average quoted
as casual context in a discussion message, inside the paragraph explaining why
numbers must not be supplied from nothing. They had the correct output on screen
and transcribed a different figure seconds later. A rule scoped to reports leaves
that uncovered, and it is the case that best demonstrates the failure.

Their reading is right and is evidenced by both instances: reports are where a
fabricated number does the most damage, because the checkable material around it
lends it credit; passing mentions are where it is most likely to happen, because
nobody is careful in a sentence that is not the point of the message.

Two changes, and the section should not get longer:

- widen the scope to any prose quoting a measurement, while keeping "report" as
  the named high-damage case;
- add the mechanical mitigation they proposed, which is the part that actually
  works: capture the figure in the same invocation as the result rather than
  transcribing it. Both instances happened to people actively writing about this
  exact failure, so vigilance is demonstrably not the defence. It is the
  measurement-shaped analogue of preferring an effect over a spelling of it.

Constraint: this must replace the existing sentences rather than accumulate. The
section has grown five times tonight and I said the next addition should trade
against something; this is that addition.
creator: sonance:pi-daemon:sonance-pi-daemon-pidm-pico-on-demand-dev-test-son

title: Add Attic-backed aarch64 CI and move consumer acceptance out of install gates
description:
Operator-directed 2026-08-02 follow-up after native/emulated aarch64 Nix installs failed load-sensitive consumer/integration tests.

Current truth at true main 810f19a:
- Pi Daemon CI uses cachix/install-nix-action only; it has no Attic login/use/pull/push step and publishes no package closure.
- Linux x86_64 and macOS CI run `nix flake check --print-build-logs`; both passed at 810f19a.
- flake `checks.package` is the package, so `nix flake check` builds it. buildNpmPackage runs `npm test` for non-aarch64-linux, and doInstallCheck always runs installed version checks plus `test/consumer-acceptance.test.mjs` against the packaged wrapper.
- aarch64-linux deliberately disables the broad Node check under emulation, but still runs consumer acceptance. Native/emulated builds reproduced: daemon socket absent after the named 120s hang bound; descendant negative control observed only one of child+grandchild after a fixed 500ms wait. Current main still contains both assumptions, so latest CI green does not structurally fix the race.
- docs/operations.md already mandates an off-device aarch64-linux binfmt build and manual `attic push -j1 SERVER:collective`; CI does not implement it.

Deliver:
1. Remove process/timing-heavy `consumer-acceptance.test.mjs` from the standard `npm test` glob and from package installCheck. Keep deterministic installed `pi-daemon version` and `pi-daemon-rpc --version` checks in installCheck. Add an explicit script for consumer acceptance.
2. Add a separate scheduled + workflow_dispatch acceptance workflow. It is non-blocking with respect to push/install gates. Run consumer acceptance on suitable real x86 Linux and/or the packaged target; retain logs. On failure, invoke the configured feedback/bead webhook path (token/URL from environment secrets) to file/dedupe a triage bead rather than making ordinary installs red. If feedback credentials are absent, report clearly and retain an artifact; do not expose tokens.
3. Add a heavy aarch64-linux closure job on self-hosted `[self-hosted, nix, x86_64-linux]` with binfmt. Configure private Attic as an additive signed substituter before build, so dependencies/prior closure pull from cache. Build exact `.#packages.aarch64-linux.pi-daemon`, verify the installed aarch64 binaries under emulation with deterministic version checks, then push the resulting output closure to Attic so Nix-on-Droid consumers substitute it later.
4. title: Fail packaged-SPA tests with an explicit missing-build diagnostic instead of 404 vs 200
description:
Running a single packaged-SPA test after only `tsc` (rather than the full
`npm run build`, which also runs `web:build`) fails as a bare
`AssertionError: 404 !== 200` with no hint that `dist/dashboard/index.html`
is simply absent. Observed on `test/dashboard-server.test.mjs` ->
"instance YAML constructs the same secure server without exposing a daemon
bearer", which fetches `/dash/` and expects the packaged index; the other 15
tests in the file pass because they write their own temporary assets dir.

Cost: the failure looks like a real regression during a refactor, so it burns
a full build cycle to disprove. `npm run test:unit` is documented as the
build-free loop, which makes the trap easy to hit.

Suggested shape (mirrors bd-f786ca's structured CLI exit diagnostics): add a
shared precondition helper for the small number of assertions that depend on
the packaged SPA, so a missing `dist/dashboard/index.html` fails with an
explicit "packaged Dash SPA missing - run `npm run build`" message instead of
a status-code mismatch. Skipping is not proposed; the gate should still fail,
just legibly.

Filed via reflect-session mixin from bd-ad9ef9 session.

Still reproduces on main at 34f18a8, verified rather than assumed: removing
`dist/dashboard` and running the file gives

    ✖ instance YAML constructs the same secure server without exposing a daemon bearer
      AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:
      404 !== 200

with no mention of the packaged SPA. The other tests in the file pass, so the
failure looks like a targeted regression in that one scenario.

Partly mitigated since filing, but not where it matters. `bd-acd227` gave
`scripts/postbuild.mjs` an explicit line when `web/dist` is absent, so anyone
arriving via `npm run build:src` is told. That does not cover the path this bead
describes: `npm run test:unit` builds nothing at all, so postbuild never runs and
the only signal is the status-code mismatch.

The fix therefore still wants to be in the assertion rather than the build. A
check that `dist/dashboard/index.html` exists before fetching `/dash/`, failing
with the build command named, would cover both routes and cost nothing on a
normal run. Note the related draft bd-b771c1, which asks for stale-`dist`
detection in the same build-free loop — the two are adjacent and a single
fixture-side check may serve both, though they are different failures: this one
is an absent artefact, that one is a present but outdated artefact.

Post-close receipt correction (shell-safe stdin body): landed and verified on true GitHub main at 7c06e91. Added shared assertPackagedDashboardBuilt precondition for the one instance-YAML DashboardServer acceptance that intentionally serves repository dist/dashboard. Missing or directory-shaped dist/dashboard/index.html now hard-fails before server startup with a bounded path-free message naming npm run build; this is never a skip. Other dashboard-server tests keep their temporary assets. Added four direct negative/positive controls and documented the build-free loop in CONTRIBUTING, PLAN, and CHANGELOG. Manual negative control temporarily moved dist/dashboard, ran the real scenario, observed exit 1 with the explicit packaged-SPA-missing remediation and no bare 404-vs-200 assertion, restored with a shell trap, and asserted the index returned. Receipts: npm test 525/525, nix flake check exit 0, post-rebase helper 4/4 and real packaged scenario 1/1.

title: Check the instrument before trusting its disagreement, when a sweep is verified twice
description:
Twice tonight a mechanical sweep was verified by an audit that derived the
expected result from `origin/main` and compared it against the converted source
— bd-95635b for ownership, bd-568050 for exposure. Both times the audit was
right. The second time I also ran an independent recount, and it disagreed. The
recount was what was wrong: `grep -v` applied after `-o` filters the matched
strings, not the filenames, so the predicate module's own policy literals were
counted.

That was thirty seconds to spot because the numbers were small and the direction
of the error was obvious. It would not have been if the sweep were larger, and
the failure mode is unpleasant: a verification that disagrees invites you to
distrust the change, which is the more expensive thing to re-examine.

Both audits were also thrown away afterwards, correctly — they compare against a
moving reference (see the earlier draft on migration-time verification). So the
knowledge of how to verify a sweep of this shape currently exists only in two
commit messages.

Suggested shape, small and cheap:

- a short note in CONTRIBUTING beside the negative-controls section: when a
  mechanical sweep is verified by a second instrument, check the instrument
  against a case whose answer is known before trusting its disagreement. The
  cheapest version is to run it against the unconverted tree and confirm it
  reports zero mismatches, which exercises the extraction on both sides;
- and the observation that the two audits shared a structure — derive expected
  from the old tree, compare against emitted policy in the new — which is worth
  naming as a pattern if a third sweep of this kind appears.

Not proposing a reusable harness. Two instances is not enough to know the shape
generalises, and the audits were ten lines each.

Filed via reflect-session mixin from bd-568050 session.

title: [broken-on-main] npm test fails: e2e:nix script asserted by exact string, preflight legitimately added
description:
`npm test` is red on main. `test/playwright-browser-resolution.test.mjs` asserts the `e2e:nix` npm script by exact string equality:

```
actual:   'node scripts/check-playwright-browsers.mjs && node scripts/check-browser-launch.mjs && playwright test'
expected: 'node scripts/check-playwright-browsers.mjs && playwright test'
```

bd-e3fa3e correctly inserted the launch preflight into that script. The test is wrong, not the change: a correct addition to a pipeline should not fail a test that claims to check "the repository wires one documented Nix path". Nothing about the property it is named for was violated.

This is mine, filed and fixed by the same agent that wrote it. It is also the exact fragility flagged in the draft about tests asserting repository source text — an assertion that pins a literal string turns any legitimate edit into a behavioural failure, and here it did so within an hour of the string changing.

Fix: assert the properties that matter rather than the literal. The script must run the browsers preflight before anything else, must end by invoking `playwright test`, and must chain with `&&` so a failed preflight stops the run. Additional preflight steps between those points are legitimate and must not fail the test. Same treatment for the `e2e:check` assertion beside it.

Not in scope, but worth noting for whoever picks up the source-text draft: this file also matches `flake.nix` source text for the e2e shell wiring, which survived the alejandra reformat by luck rather than design.

title: Give fail-closed assertions a negative control, so a vacuous pass cannot hide
description:
Three assertions were found tonight that were green while verifying nothing, in
three unrelated areas, by three different accidents:

- `web/e2e/dash.spec.ts` compared `scrollTop` before and after a presentation
  switch, but read it immediately after `page.goto`, so it was comparing two
  pre-hydration zeros (fixed in bd-94d7df).
- `test/dashboard-identity-config.test.mjs` created a deliberately
  group-readable credential with `writeFile`'s mode argument, which the ambient
  umask masks. Under a restrictive umask the file came out owner-only, so the
  fail-closed assertion had nothing to reject and passed (fixed in bd-7cba4b).
  `test/bootstrap.test.mjs` had the same latent defect.
- `test/playwright-browser-resolution.test.mjs` asserted a script by exact
  string equality, so it was checking a spelling rather than the property its
  name claimed (fixed in bd-228b91).

What they have in common is that none would have been caught by reading the
test. Each was exposed only when an environment differed slightly from the one
it was written in — a loaded host, a hardened runner, a legitimately extended
pipeline. The umask one is the most uncomfortable: had the umask been
restrictive everywhere, that security assertion would have been green from the
day it was written while never exercising the check at all.

Proposal: a negative control for assertions whose value is that they reject
something. Once, at authoring time, break the property deliberately, watch the
test fail, restore it, and say so in a comment or the commit message. It is
seconds of work and it is the only step that would have caught all three.

Where it should apply, in rough order:

1. Fail-closed and permission assertions — anything asserting that a mode, an
   owner, a credential, or a path is rejected. These are the cases where a
   vacuous pass is a silent loss of security coverage.
2. Acceptance assertions that compare a measurement before and after an action,
   where "before" may not have settled.
3. Structural assertions over repository text, where the check may be pinned to
   a spelling rather than a property (see also bd-dff2d8).

Not proposing a mechanism or a lint — a convention line in CONTRIBUTING beside
the existing test guidance is probably the whole change. The value is the habit,
not the enforcement.

Observed jointly with pidm-pi-on-demand-dev-test-son, who independently
identified the same class from the other two instances.

title: Group CI failures by their error class, not by co-occurrence in one run
description:
Two tests failed the Node CI lane in the same run, and the bead filed for it
attributed both to a missing `openssl`. Only one was.

    not ok 97  dedicated web CLI ...                    Error: spawn openssl ENOENT
    not ok 102 provider documents and credential ...    Missing expected rejection.
    not ok 143 loads bounded owner-controlled TLS ...   Error: spawn openssl ENOENT

Test 102's cause is unrelated: `writeFile(path, value, { mode: 0o644 })` has its
mode masked by the ambient umask, so on a runner with a restrictive one the
deliberately group-readable credential is created owner-only and the fail-closed
assertion has nothing to reject. Reproduced locally with `umask 077`.

The reason this is worth a bead rather than just a fix: co-occurring failures in
one CI run invite a single explanation, and the bead's own evidence section
listed test 102 under the openssl heading without checking its error text. The
distinguishing information was one line away in the same log — `Missing expected
rejection` is not an ENOENT — and the failing assertion's line number was in the
stack.

Suggested shape, cheap end first:

1. A line in the broken-on-main workflow in CONTRIBUTING or the dev profile:
   when several tests fail in one run, read each failure's own error before
   grouping them, because a shared lane is not a shared cause.
2. Possibly a triage helper that prints one line per failing test with its error
   class extracted from the run record, so grouping is done on the errors rather
   than on adjacency in the log.

title: Document clean-install check after dependency-changing rebases
description:
While validating bd-5f9ca1 after rebasing onto bd-2756e4, the checkout's stale `node_modules` produced TS2307 for a newly added exact root dependency even though `package.json` and `package-lock.json` were correct. This was initially misclassified as broken main and caused avoidable peer routing; `npm ci --ignore-scripts` resolved the import, after which only the owning lane's genuine ambient package-root test issue remained. Add an actionable contributor/agent check: when a rebase changes npm dependency metadata and compilation reports an unresolved new package, compare root package/lock and run the clean exact-lock install before filing broken-on-main. Preserve the separate rule that source or lock omissions still route to the owning bead. Filed via reflect-session mixin from bd-5f9ca1 session.

## Second reproduction, different agent, same night

Rebasing onto the Pi SDK 0.82.1 migration (`5c173ec`, bd-a3b8aa) and running `npm run build` produced five type errors in `src/pi-sdk-contract.ts` — new session event types not assignable to the SDK's union, and both `IsExact` assertions unsatisfied. It presents as a broken migration in a file the rebasing agent did not touch.

It was stale `node_modules`: the lockfile pinned 0.82.1 while the tree still had 0.80.6 installed, so the pinned contract inventory was being checked against the previous SDK's types. `npm ci --ignore-scripts` cleared it, the build was clean, and the compatibility suite passed 5/5 against the landed migration. Nothing was wrong with what had landed.

Both instances tonight nearly produced a misdirected report to the agent who landed the change, and one of them did. That is the cost worth naming in the check: not the lost minutes, but a peer being told their work is broken when the reporter's install state is what is stale.

The tell is specific enough to write down: type errors naming a contract the current change did not touch, immediately after a rebase that crossed a lockfile change, are an install-state question before they are a code question. `node -e 'console.log(require("./node_modules/<dep>/package.json").version)'` against the version in `package.json` settles it in one command, which is cheaper than reading the diff.

title: docs/dash-e2e.md asserts an unsupported cause for the one unexplained full-suite failure
description:
docs/dash-e2e.md currently states, in the full-suite gating section, that the one multi-scenario failure observed during bd-65fddd validation was "a starvation cascade". That label is an inference, not an observation, and the run output was not preserved, so it cannot be tested.

A peer working bd-df1c84 proposes a better-supported explanation: six scenarios failing in under a second each is the signature of the browser process dying at launch, which Playwright surfaces as `browserContext.newPage: Target page, context or browser has been closed`. A slow scenario burns its timeout rather than failing in 476ms. The same signature appeared for all three @smoke scenarios in CI run 30412617437.

Subsequent evidence, with full logs retained: two further full-suite runs at load average 14.1 were 21/21 and 21/21, with zero occurrences of `Target page, context or browser has been closed`, `browserType.launch`, or `Target closed`, and /dev/shm at 85M used of 7.7G before and 79M after. Post-fix the record is 5 of 6 full runs green with one unclassifiable failure and no reproduction in five attempts.

Rewrite that passage to state what is known: one unexplained failure of six scenarios in under a second each, two candidate explanations (browser launch failure, host contention) with the launch signature named so a future observer can classify it in one grep, and the fact that it did not reproduce in five subsequent runs. The operational conclusion is unchanged — do not promote CI to full-suite gating until that failure is explained — but it must rest on an unexplained observation rather than on an invented mechanism.

title: Record the measurement form of vacuity, and the hazard in performing a manual mutation
description:
Two additions to CONTRIBUTING's "Negative controls" section, both from tonight
and both offered by the agents who found them.

**The class behind the instances.** The section currently describes assertions
that pass while checking nothing. The same error occurs in measurements, and
three of tonight's findings are it at different scales:

- a fixture reported a mode nobody checked was the mode requested;
- 41 ownership guards had a 100% pass rate because none could fire;
- the macOS job's 6-successes-in-30 record was counted without asking whether a
  runner carrying its labels existed at all.

Stated generally: counting outcomes tells you the distribution of what happened,
not whether the thing you are counting is capable of happening. pico-dev-test-son
put the specific rule in the CI note — do not assume a job that never reports is
flaky, check a runner exists — and asked that the general form live here instead,
since it is about assertions and measurements rather than about CI.

**A hazard in performing form 3.** The manual mutation shipped as the change in
bd-b225fa, through two independent mistakes that both had to hold: the file was
restored with `git checkout` while already staged, which restores from the index
and therefore reverted nothing, and the verification piped `nix build` through
`tail`, so the exit status checked belonged to `tail`. The negative control
became the defect.

Form 3 is already the weakest form; it should carry the two things that make it
survivable — restore from `HEAD` rather than the index, and check the status of
the command being verified rather than a pipeline's last stage.

**A distinct failure worth naming separately.** A guard that verifies something
true of every value except the one it was pointed at is not the same as a guard
that verifies nothing. It fails in the safe direction — red immediately rather
than green for a night — and the remedy differs: the vacuous one needs a negative
case, this one needed its exemption to live where the guard could see it rather
than in a comment beside it.

Scope: the section text, and whatever the section's own test needs so the
addition is pinned the way the ordering is.

- cite the bd-228b91 mutations under form 3, where they honestly belong, as an

title: Playwright webServer timeout is shorter than the build it runs, so the first e2e run always times out
description:
`web/playwright.config.ts` sets `webServer.timeout` to 30s while
`webServer.command` is `npm run build && npm run preview`. The build alone takes
about 32s on a busy node, so the very first `npm run web:e2e` reliably fails
with "Timed out waiting 30000ms from config.webServer" before a single test
runs. Nothing in the message points at the build being the slow part, so it
reads as a broken harness.

Two cheap options: raise the timeout to something the build comfortably fits in,
or make it env-overridable the way `DASH_TEST_PORT` already is.

Related, and a bigger time sink: the Playwright browser revision is pinned by
the npm `@playwright/test` version (1.61.1 wants chromium 1228) while the Nix
browser bundle on this node provides 1223. The failure surfaces as
"Executable doesn't exist ... run npx playwright install", which is misleading
inside a Nix-provided environment where downloading is not the intended fix. The
bd-185516 preflight now catches version drift, which is the right shape; this
note is about the adjacent build-timeout trap that sits in front of it.

Observed while validating bd-94d7df, which needed a real browser run to find the
root cause at all.

Filed via reflect-session mixin from bd-94d7df session.

title: Capability-gate supervisord stopwaitsecs for Nix-on-Droid
description:
Nix-on-Droid evaluation fails because Pi Daemon's Home Manager module unconditionally emits `supervisord.programs.<service>.stopwaitsecs`, but the active typed schema from collective-public/modules/supervisord-program-options.nix does not define that option and its config renderer does not output it. The Pi Daemon module check masks the mismatch by stubbing `supervisord.programs` as attrsOf anything, and even asserts the unsupported field.

Fix Pi Daemon compatibility now: introspect the imported supervisord programs element suboptions and include stopwaitsecs only when supported. Keep command, environment, autorestart, startsecs, stopsignal and log options unchanged. Replace permissive test stub with a strict schema matching current Nix-on-Droid options; prove evaluation succeeds and stopwaitsecs is absent. Add a second schema that exposes stopwaitsecs and prove Pi Daemon emits the rounded graceful timeout there, preserving forward compatibility when Collective gains support. Document fallback to supervisor's own default when the schema lacks the option.

title: Invoke npm retry helper through pinned Nix Bash; /usr/bin/env is absent in the build sandbox
description:
# bd-833b3e — Nix sandbox pinned-Bash source blocker

## Hosted evidence

Exact run `30810507444` and later run `30811475306`, both containing the closure
publisher source, fail before hydration on both Linux targets:

```
.../stdenv-linux/setup:
.../prefetch-npm-deps-retry.sh: /usr/bin/env: bad interpreter: No such file or directory
builder failed with exit code 126
```

`nix/npm-deps.nix` executes the repository script directly:

```nix
${../scripts/prefetch-npm-deps-retry.sh} "$srcLockfile" "$out"
```

Its `#!/usr/bin/env bash` is valid on a host shell but `/usr/bin/env` does not
exist inside the Nix build sandbox. The prior `bd-94a9d2` npm staging fix does not
patch this call site.

## Fix

Invoke through pinned Nix Bash:

```nix
${pkgs.bash}/bin/bash ${../scripts/prefetch-npm-deps-retry.sh} "$srcLockfile" "$out"
```

Add a source regression assertion proving the Nix expression contains the pinned
Bash invocation and does not directly execute the script.

## Validation

Disposable clone of current pi-daemon main:

- new focused regression test: PASS
- `nix eval .#packages.x86_64-linux.pi-daemon.drvPath --raw`: PASS
  (`/nix/store/13q55...-pi-daemon-0.3.0.drv`)

The existing broader `npm-deps-retry.test.mjs` suite cannot run on helsinki
outside a compatibility shell because its own fixture invokes `/bin/bash`, which
is absent on NixOS. That is pre-existing and separate; do not report the full
suite as passing from this node. Hosted delivery lane remains authoritative.

## Exact diff

diff --git a/nix/npm-deps.nix b/nix/npm-deps.nix
index 55c21cb..b2c3983 100644
--- a/nix/npm-deps.nix
+++ b/nix/npm-deps.nix
@@ -44,7 +44,10 @@ in
       export outputHash=${pkgs.lib.escapeShellArg hash}
       export PI_DAEMON_NPM_FETCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS=${toString maxAttempts}
       export PI_DAEMON_NPM_FETCH_INITIAL_BACKOFF_SECS=${toString initialBackoffSecs}
-      ${../scripts/prefetch-npm-deps-retry.sh} "$srcLockfile" "$out"
+      # bd-833b3e: execute through the pinned Nix bash. Calling the source
+      # script directly delegates to `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, but `/usr/bin/env`
+      # does not exist inside the Nix build sandbox (hosted jobs fail 126).
+      ${pkgs.bash}/bin/bash ${../scripts/prefetch-npm-deps-retry.sh} "$srcLockfile" "$out"
 
       runHook postBuild
     '';
diff --git a/test/npm-deps-retry.test.mjs b/test/npm-deps-retry.test.mjs
index b0e1e43..0a0e02f 100644
--- a/test/npm-deps-retry.test.mjs
+++ b/test/npm-deps-retry.test.mjs
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@ import { promisify } from "node:util";
 
 const run = promisify(execFile);
 const retryScript = new URL("../scripts/prefetch-npm-deps-retry.sh", import.meta.url).pathname;
+const npmDepsNix = new URL("../nix/npm-deps.nix", import.meta.url).pathname;
 
 async function fixture(t, mode) {
   const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "pi-daemon-npm-retry-"));
@@ -88,6 +89,19 @@ async function exists(path) {
   }
 }
 
+
+test("Nix build invokes the retry script through pinned bash, not its env shebang", async () => {
+  const source = await readFile(npmDepsNix, "utf8");
+  assert.match(
+    source,
+    /\$\{pkgs\.bash\}\/bin\/bash \$\{\.\.\/scripts\/prefetch-npm-deps-retry\.sh\}/,
+  );
+  assert.doesNotMatch(
+    source,
+    /^\s*\$\{\.\.\/scripts\/prefetch-npm-deps-retry\.sh\}/m,
+  );

title: Make the session-dir drift alarm state its decision, not just its condition
description:
The `PI_SDK_EXPORTS_DEFAULT_SESSION_DIR` drift alarm in `test/pi-sdk-compatibility.test.mjs` fires when Pi's package root starts exporting `getDefaultSessionDir`. Its failure message currently reads:

    Pi's exported surface drifted: update PI_SDK_EXPORTS_DEFAULT_SESSION_DIR and
    consume the upstream helper in src/pi-sdk-contract.ts

That message invites the cheap response. Flipping the constant turns the suite green and leaves the question unasked, and the message reads as though the flip is the fix with the adoption as an afterthought. An agent mid-migration, with a dozen other assertions to update, will do the half that makes it green.

The decision the alarm exists to force is already worked out in the module's doc comment and should be *in* the failure message: upstream's helper calls `mkdirSync` as a side effect, while the daemon requires a side-effect-free derivation because it creates every session directory owner-private with repair. So a creating helper means keep the local reproduction and demote the export to a conformance oracle; only a path-only variant should be consumed and the reproduction deleted.

Observed live: the Pi 0.82.1 migration (bd-a3b8aa) reached this alarm, which stayed quiet because 0.82.1 still does not export the helper. The migrating agent verified the underlying fact rather than trusting the green assertion, and separately named the general property — both this alarm and the pinned contract unions are built so that the cheap response destroys the signal, and in both cases the expensive response found something. That is the argument for making the expensive response the one the message describes.

Scope is one message string plus a comment. Worth doing while the reasoning is fresh rather than when it next fires, which by construction is during a migration when nobody has time to reconstruct it.

title: Adopt the exposure policy at the mode-check call sites
description:
Follow-up to bd-aa2f90, which named and censused the mode axis but did not convert the call sites, exactly as bd-9ad9e5 did for ownership before bd-95635b adopted it.

`src/path-ownership.ts` now carries `PathExposurePolicy` (`private` for `0o077`, `no-foreign-writers` for `0o022`), `hasForbiddenExposure`, and a combined `PathTrustPolicy` whose `exposure` is optional so authority-to-act checks keep taking no view on mode. `test/path-ownership.test.mjs` pins every mask literal per module. The ~40 call sites still open-code `(info.mode & 0o077) !== 0`.

Adoption would make the tested predicate authoritative rather than parallel, as it did for ownership. Three things make this sweep different from that one, and worth doing carefully:

1. The optional third shape. Three sites — `server.ts` refusing to replace a socket it does not own, `session-inventory.ts` skipping foreign entries in a scan — have no mask and must not acquire one. A sweep that gives every ownership check an exposure policy is wrong, not merely noisy.
2. The nine sites pairing a strict owner with a lax mask are the ones most likely to be "corrected" by mistake during a mechanical pass. Each is deliberate: only the current user may have written this session state, but others reading it is not the property being protected.
3. `dashboard-tls.ts` applies both masks in one module, to the certificate and the key, so a per-module policy would be wrong there. Per-path, as the type already assumes.

Suggested approach mirrors what worked for ownership: convert one module per commit, keep every error type and message byte-identical, verify each site's old mask against its new policy mechanically rather than by eye, and update the census in the same change so the count moves from open-coded to adopted rather than disappearing. A closing invariant worth adding: no `0o077` or `0o022` literal remains in `src/` outside `path-ownership.ts`.

title: Assert the e2e shell contract by evaluation instead of matching flake source text
description:
Worked example for form 1 of the negative-control convention, requested by the agent holding that bead.

`test/playwright-browser-resolution.test.mjs` asserts `flake.nix` source text — that `e2e = pkgs.mkShell` appears and that three environment variables are assigned — plus a `Justfile` recipe name. Those are proxies for the property, not the property. The same file already broke once tonight (bd-228b91) from exactly this coupling, and its flake assertions survived the alejandra reformat by luck rather than construction.

The effect is directly observable:

```
nix eval --raw .#devShells.x86_64-linux.e2e.PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH
nix eval --raw .#devShells.x86_64-linux.e2e.PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD
nix eval --raw .#devShells.x86_64-linux.e2e.PI_DAEMON_PLAYWRIGHT_DRIVER_VERSION
```

Replace the text matching with a `nix flake check` derivation that asserts what the shell exports. Two constraints make this non-trivial and both belong in the convention:

1. Interpolating the browsers path into a check puts the 2.1 GiB Playwright closure in its build inputs, so a check that previously cost nothing would fetch the bundle on every run. The string context must be discarded; the check asserts the shell's contract, not the bundle's contents.
2. The evaluation needs Nix, and the Node gate deliberately does not have it. So the assertion moves lane, from `npm test` to `nix flake check`, rather than being rewritten in place.

Worth adding while there: assert that the driver version the shell exports equals the `@playwright/test` version pinned in `web/package.json`. The runtime preflight already enforces that, but asserting it at evaluation time means a dependency bump that breaks the pin fails the Nix lane immediately instead of at the first browser run.

Keep the package.json script-shape assertions in the Node gate. Those read the scripts themselves, which is the effect rather than a proxy for it.

title: Require every figure in a verification report to come from the run reported
description:
One sentence for the measurement paragraph of CONTRIBUTING's negative-controls
section, proposed by pico-dev-test-son after I broadcast a verification report
containing one figure I had not measured.

The report gave build time, suite counts, check results, and a host load average.
Everything but the load average was read off the run. That number I wrote before
measuring, then measured, and did not go back and correct before sending.

Their observation is the part worth recording: a fabricated figure inside an
otherwise-observed report is more dangerous than a wrong one standing alone,
because everything around it is checkable and true, so a reader extends that
credibility to the one number nobody measured. Which is the same shape as the
vacuous assertion — the surrounding structure is sound, and that is exactly why
nobody looks at the part that is not.

The rule they suggest is narrow enough to follow: every figure in a verification
report comes from the run being reported, or it is not stated. Not "check your
numbers", which is unactionable; "if you did not read it off this run, leave it
out".

Scope: one or two sentences on the existing measurement paragraph, not a new
subsection. The section has grown four times tonight and each addition looked
justified on its own, which is itself a reason to keep this one short.

title: ensurePrivateDirectory fails closed on owner-owned 0755 dirs, causing permanent host restart loop
description:
Observed on the ms-dev-5 operator instance `pi-daemon-daemon-main.service`: a
permanent restart loop, 377 consecutive failures, every start ending in

    {"level":"error","event":"pi_daemon_fatal","errorCode":"insecure_state_path",
     "message":"Pi sessions data root must be owner-only"}

## Root cause

`ensurePrivateDirectory()` in `src/durability.ts` creates with `mkdir(path,
{recursive: true, mode: 0o700})` and then *rejects* any pre-existing directory
whose mode has `& 0o077` set. `mkdir` does not chmod a directory that already
exists, so the constructor is fail-closed but never self-healing.

The failing path was `~/.pi/agent/sessions`, mode `0755`, owned by the current
user. It reached `0755` because the instance runs with
`--agent-dir ~/.pi/agent`, which is the *shared* Pi agent directory that plain
`pi` also writes. Plain `pi` creates `sessions/` and its per-project children
with a default `umask 022`, i.e. `0755`.

This is not a one-off: any plain `pi` run that creates a new project session
directory re-introduces a `0755` directory under the shared root. The same
check also guards `"Pi project session directory"` in
`src/session-ownership.ts`, so new project dirs can fail session open even
after the root is repaired.

Note the mode `0755` granted no real access here: the parent `~/.pi/agent` was
already `0700`, so nothing outside the owner could traverse into `sessions/` in
the first place. The host refused to start over a permission bit that was not
actually exposing anything.

## Repair applied on ms-dev-5

`chmod 700` on `~/.pi/agent/sessions` and its subdirectories. The service then
reached `pi_daemon_ready` on the next restart and has stayed up. No config,
unit, or Nix change was involved.

## Suggested fix

In `ensurePrivateDirectory`, when the directory exists, is a real directory,
and `info.uid === process.getuid()`, `chmod` it to `0700` instead of throwing.
Keep failing closed for the cases that actually indicate compromise or
misconfiguration: symlink, non-directory, or wrong owner. An owner-owned
directory that is merely too permissive is exactly the case the daemon can
safely and idempotently correct, and correcting it removes a startup failure
mode that no operator action can durably prevent while the agent directory is
shared with plain `pi`.

Consider also whether `--agent-dir` should default to a daemon-private
directory rather than the shared `~/.pi/agent`, so host startup does not depend
on another writer's umask.

title: Ownership and permission mode are two independent axes, and only one of them is a named policy
description:
**Retitled and rewritten. This bead originally claimed that the permission masks encode the config-versus-secret distinction a second time. That claim was refuted by pidm-pico-on-demand-dev-test-son, who checked the correlation before acting on it; the corrected model below is theirs. The bead is kept as the record because a companion filing carrying the same model was not visible on the board at the time of writing, and a refutation nobody can find is worth less than the wrong claim it corrects.**

Original claim: the `0o077` / `0o022` split encodes the same config-versus-secret distinction as the root exemption, so the permission axis is that policy written a second time as scattered literals.

That does not hold. Correlating every adopted site's ownership policy against its nearest mask:

```
owner-only    + 0o077        22
owner-or-root + 0o022         9
owner-only    + 0o022         9   <- refutes the correlation
owner-only    + no mask       3
owner-or-root + both masks    1   (dashboard-tls; cert and key differ)
```

Nine sites pair a strict owner with a lax mask — session-ownership (3), session-inventory, pi-adapter's session and root paths, server, self-update's bin directory, transcript-projector's session source. Each requires the current user to own the path while tolerating that others may read it, which is coherent for session state: only I may have written this, but it need not be unreadable. That is not derivable from the ownership policy.

The corrected model is two independent axes rather than one decision written twice. Ownership answers who may have authored the material; mode answers who else may read or write it. Secrets need both strict; provisioned configuration wants a relaxed owner with a strict writer; session state wants a strict owner with a relaxed reader.

This matters because the fix implied by the original claim would have been actively harmful. Deriving the mask from the ownership policy would have quietly tightened those nine sites — accident-becomes-contract again, running in the direction that looks like an improvement, and therefore the least likely to be questioned.

The three no-mask sites are a third kind rather than a gap: `server.ts:645` refuses to replace a socket it does not own, and session-inventory skips foreign entries during a scan. They decide authority to act on a path rather than trust in material read from it, so mode is irrelevant, and a change that gave every ownership check a mask would be wrong for exactly these.

The one reassuring result: no site appears misclassified under the corrected model.

Recorded because 31 of 44 sites fit the pattern, which is close enough to look like a rule, and acting on it would have been most tempting precisely where it was wrong.

title: probe cannot verify protocol-v2 readiness
description:
`pi-daemon probe` cannot verify protocol-v2 readiness, which is exactly the readiness an external orchestrator (Cacophony) depends on.

`PiDaemonClient.handshake()` hardcodes `protocolVersion: "1.0"` (src/client.ts:157), and the server only advertises the v2 capability set when the request version starts with "2." (src/server.ts:366). So the shipped probe always reports `protocolVersion 1.0` and omits `configuredOpen`, `sessionDir`, `hostToolAdapter`, `hostToolOperationCount`, and `supportedProtocolVersions` — the precise flags that determine whether a host can accept configured opens with deterministic per-agent session storage.

Measured against a live host: `pi-daemon probe` reports protocol 1.0 with three capability keys, while a raw v2 handshake against the same socket in the same minute returns supportedProtocolVersions ["1.0","2.0"], configuredOpen true, sessionDir true, hostToolAdapter true, hostToolOperationCount 6. Operators currently have to hand-craft NDJSON over the socket to learn any of this.

Fix: negotiate the highest supported version by default and let the caller pin one explicitly, without breaking v1-only hosts. Keep the existing ready/exit-code contract.

title: Update TLS fixture contract for pinned Bash package-check dependency
description:
# bd-833b3e — update TLS fixture contract for pinned Bash check input

## Hosted evidence

Pi-daemon main `e736204` / `ca68d27` correctly fixes production and retry-fixture
Bash resolution. Main CI run `30825859803` remains red because an independent
contract test still requires the old exact list:

```js
assert.match(flake, /nativeBuildInputs = \[pkgs\.makeWrapper pkgs\.openssl\]/)
```

Adding `pkgs.bash` is correct; the contract assertion is stale. It causes both
plain Node and Nix checks to fail, preventing hosted acceptance before closure
publisher execution.

## Fix

Update the exact assertion to:

```js
/nativeBuildInputs = \[pkgs\.makeWrapper pkgs\.openssl pkgs\.bash\]/
```

Comment why Bash is a check dependency: NixOS/sandbox has neither `/bin/bash` nor
an exported BASH; package checks need pinned Bash on PATH.

## Validation in disposable current-main clone

- full `test/tls-fixture-contract.test.mjs`: 5/5 PASS
- Nix package derivation eval: PASS
  `/nix/store/yzjny5w73kh5xhzlzsm55kr4579bnd3h-pi-daemon-0.3.0.drv`
- one-file exact scope; no canonical checkout/host mutation

## Exact diff

diff --git a/test/tls-fixture-contract.test.mjs b/test/tls-fixture-contract.test.mjs
index 3f3cb66..5cdbf5b 100644
--- a/test/tls-fixture-contract.test.mjs
+++ b/test/tls-fixture-contract.test.mjs
@@ -42,8 +42,10 @@ test("the openssl dependency is declared in every lane that runs the suite", asy
     readFile(join(repositoryRoot, "flake.nix"), "utf8"),
     readFile(join(repositoryRoot, ".github", "workflows", "ci.yml"), "utf8"),
   ]);
-  // The package build and the dev shells.
-  assert.match(flake, /nativeBuildInputs = \[pkgs\.makeWrapper pkgs\.openssl\]/);
+  // The package build and the dev shells. bd-833b3e adds pinned Bash to

title: TUI presentation reading-anchor assertion is not load-proof at its 32px tolerance
description:
`web/e2e/dash.spec.ts:563` — `expect(Math.abs(restoredAnchor - readingAnchor)).toBeLessThan(32)` in "TUI presentation streams one canonical controller grid to read-only pane mirrors" — fails intermittently in full-suite runs under host load and passes in isolation.

Reproductions on 85e41a0, node sonance:

- pidm-pico-dev-test-son, load average ~11.7: two consecutive full-suite runs, 20 passed / 1 failed, measured 43px against the 32px tolerance. Isolated `--grep 'TUI.presentation'` passes in 15.1s.
- pidm-pi-on-demand-dev-test-son, load average ~13, instrumented probe (reverted, tree clean), three runs recording `scrollHeight`/`scrollTop`/`clientHeight` at settle and again 600ms later:

```
run 1  anchors 900.0 -> 789.0   diff 111   h=24495 at both reads, dH over +600ms = 0   FAIL
run 2  anchors 1132.0 -> 1022.0 diff 110   h=24432 at both reads, dH over +600ms = 0   FAIL
run 3  anchors 1132.0 -> 1132.0 diff 0     h=24432 at both reads, dH over +600ms = 0   PASS
```

What those measurements establish:

1. The settle is not returning early. `scrollHeight` is byte-identical at settle and 600ms later in every run, so `settledDistanceFromBottom`'s three-consecutive-samples-within-1px gate is doing its job and waiting longer would change nothing.
2. `scrollHeight` and `clientHeight` are identical across the presentation switch within each failing run. Same total size, same viewport, different `scrollTop`. An earlier hypothesis on this bead — that the virtualizer's dynamic measurement lands differently across the switch — is contradicted by this and is withdrawn.
3. The error is bimodal, not noisy: 111, 110, 0. This is a discrete offset that either occurs or does not, so it is not a tolerance that needs widening. The 43px and ~110px observations are most likely the same defect landing on different boundary records.

Working hypothesis for whoever takes it: transcript rows render `RichTranscriptRecord` behind `Suspense`, so remounting the Rich layer after the switch can re-suspend and re-render some rows. If the restore is applied before those rows settle into their final heights, the anchor lands short by exactly that record's height delta while the total size converges to the same value afterwards, which matches the signature above. bd-94d7df fixed the resize-observer clearing measured heights; this looks like a second, narrower path to the same symptom.

Do not widen the tolerance. 32px is meaningful, the measurements show the tolerance is not the thing that is wrong, and a wider bound would stop catching the regression it was written for.

This scenario is deliberately excluded from the CI `@smoke` subset and is recorded in `docs/dash-e2e.md` as the single blocker against gating CI on the full browser suite. Filed via reflect-session mixin from the bd-c08a07 session; measurements contributed by pidm-pi-on-demand-dev-test-son.

title: brace-expansion 5.0.7 is vulnerable to a newer advisory than the one it fixed
description:
`brace-expansion` 5.0.7 is vulnerable to GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg, a high-severity
unbounded-expansion DoS with range `<=5.0.7`. This is a **different advisory**
from GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp, which 5.0.7 fixed. The version that resolved the old
finding is the last version covered by the new one.

Measured on the lockfile after the 0.82.1 migration landed (5c173ec), not
inferred from release notes:

  npm audit: 1 advisory
    brace-expansion  high  <=5.0.7  GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg
    node: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/brace-expansion
    installed: 5.0.7

**The upstream ask is cheap, and worth stating precisely.** The SDK's published
`npm-shrinkwrap.json` pins `brace-expansion` at 5.0.7, but nothing requires that
version: the only dependant is `minimatch`, whose range is `^5.0.5`. 5.0.8 is
published and satisfies it. So this needs a shrinkwrap regeneration and a
republish, not a code change or a dependency bump in Pi.

**We cannot fix it from here, and should not appear to.** `npm audit fix
--dry-run` reports 0 added, 0 removed, 0 changed: a shipped
`npm-shrinkwrap.json` is authoritative for its own subtree, so root `overrides`
and lock edits do not replace the nested package. bd-36428f already records that
attempting root lock surgery makes audit metadata claim green while `npm ci`
still installs the vulnerable version, and that the unsafe workaround was
reverted. That reasoning applies unchanged here.

Blocks the zero-audit acceptance condition on bd-36428f, whose protobufjs half
is now satisfied: after the 0.82.1 migration the protobufjs moderate finding is
gone and the SDK resolves 7.6.5.

No external untrusted glob/pattern input path into the nested `minimatch` has
been established, so treat as dependency-availability risk pending upstream, the
same posture bd-36428f took.


## Local half landed; bead deliberately left open

`5f5c832` adds the guard against the workaround rather than the fix, because the fix is not ours to make. Any root `overrides` entry naming a package the SDK's shipped shrinkwrap owns now fails `test/pi-sdk-compatibility.test.mjs`, with the reason and the real repair in the failure text. Verified by re-adding the reverted workaround and watching it fire, not by reading the assertion. `SECURITY.md` records the finding, why it cannot be fixed locally, and why the workaround is worse than the finding it hides.

Everything in the report above was re-measured before acting on it: `npm audit` reports the single high finding at `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/brace-expansion` with 5.0.7 installed; the SDK's `minimatch@10.2.5` requires `^5.0.5`; `brace-expansion@5.0.8` is published and satisfies that range; `npm audit fix --dry-run` reports 0 added, 0 removed, 0 changed.

Left open and unclaimed. The acceptance condition is a truthful zero-audit baseline, and a guard against faking one does not deliver one — only an upstream shrinkwrap regeneration does. Closing this against the work that landed would make `closed` mean "someone worked on it", which is the property that makes a board untrustworthy.

What would close it: the SDK republishing with `brace-expansion` at 5.0.8 in its shrinkwrap, then a bump here and a clean `npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm audit` showing zero. Until then this is dependency-availability risk pending upstream, with no established untrusted glob or pattern input path into the nested `minimatch`.

2026-07-29 BLOCKER RE-VALIDATED by pidm-pico-on-demand-dev-test-son. The upstream ask is not awaiting a decision; it was never triaged.

Two issues already exist and both are CLOSED:
- earendil-works/pi#7090 "Regenerate 0.82.x shrinkwrap with brace-expansion 5.0.8+"
- earendil-works/pi#7162 "Update packaged brace-expansion to 5.0.8"

#7162 was closed within its first comment by policy, not on merit: "This issue was auto-closed. All issues from new contributors are auto-closed by default. Maintainers review auto-closed issues daily and reopen worthwhile ones ... If a maintainer replies `lgtmi` on one of your issues, your future issues will stay open. If a maintainer replies `lgtm`, your future issues and PRs will stay open."

Neither was reopened. Checked the consequence rather than assuming it, by unpacking the published tarball:

    @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.83.0 shrinkwrap:
      brace-expansion 5.0.7   (still vulnerable to GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg)
      protobufjs      7.6.5   (the 0.82.1 fix holds)
      entries missing integrity: 3 — pi-agent-core, pi-ai, pi-tui

So 0.83.0 does not resolve this bead, and upgrading to it buys nothing here. It also confirms the shrinkwrap-integrity omission is not specific to 0.82.1, so `npm run lock:repair-integrity` stays necessary across releases.

Consequence for this bead's shape: it is blocked on an untriaged report from an account without the upstream trust marker, not on a maintainer's decision. A third issue from the same account would auto-close identically. Escalating under a human identity, or opening a PR, is an operator decision rather than a worker one, so it is presented as a choice rather than actioned.

title: [broken-on-main] bootstrap-cli serve exit status failing
description:
On main d6cd751, node --test test/bootstrap-cli.test.mjs reproducibly fails at line 95: child exitCode is null rather than 0 after SIGTERM. Full npm test otherwise passes. Agent bd-6d96bb is taking the fix per broken-on-main workflow.

---

## Merged duplicate: bd-03b0d2

Title: [broken-on-main] bootstrap CLI SIGTERM race returns signal exit

`nix flake check` and a direct Nix package-check retry both fail `serve bootstraps an empty standalone instance before constructing the Pi factory` at `test/bootstrap-cli.test.mjs:95`: the child exit event reports `exitCode === null` after SIGTERM rather than graceful code 0. The exact isolated Node test and full local `npm test` pass. Root cause: `serve` publishes/listens on the owner socket before `waitForSignal()` installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers, so a client that handshakes immediately can signal during that startup window and receive the platform default termination. Add an early bounded signal latch that is installed before listeners become visible, drains through the existing whole-deadline shutdown once startup ownership exists, and is disposed on startup failure/injected shutdown. Include deterministic race coverage. Observed while validating bd-5c06cd; pre-existing on main.

title: Make closure publisher self-contained and prove effective Attic trust
description:
Hosted closure run 30761647263 at 6aff54d dispatched all four jobs. AArch64 Linux job 91533175703 passed pinned publisher shell, target/binfmt validation, Attic login/info/use, built the exact aarch64-linux package, and its Nix installCheck executed both installed version checks successfully (0.3.0, 0.3.0). The workflow then failed at line9 of the build step because `awk` is absent from mutable runner PATH while counting output paths. Workflow version/push steps were skipped; artifact 8837784570 retained build.log and output-path. Fix output parsing with Bash `mapfile`/array length (as the original aarch workflow did) or execute every required tool from the pinned publisher shell; do not add mutable runner packages.

The same build emitted repeated Nix warnings that client-specified restricted settings `netrc-file`, `require-sigs`, and `trusted-public-keys` were ignored because the runner user is not trusted. Current workflow checks `nix config show` client values, which is insufficient evidence that the daemon accepted the private cache token/key. The package appears to have built locally (including two-minute npm dependency installation), so no signed-substitution receipt exists. Make trust effective without ad-hoc runner mutation: rely on a preconfigured signed/public-read Attic substituter where appropriate, or use a supported CI Nix setup that makes the job user trusted before the already-installed-daemon short-circuit. Then add a real cache hydration/substitution proof against an exact known path and fail on ignored trust/signature warnings. Never replace cache.nixos.org and never weaken require-sigs.

X86_64 Linux job 91533175693 passed shell/target/Attic setup but exact package build failed on the separately-owned true-main deterministic gate regression service-watchdog line81; bd-801b03 fixes that at 4993ff3. Treat run30761647263 as pre-fix source evidence and rerun from >=4993ff3 after this workflow fix. Darwin jobs remained queued at observation time.

Acceptance: pinned actionlint/CI boundary tests; Bash-only exact output parsing or declared shell dependency; no `awk`/undeclared host tool; aarch package build, workflow version step and `attic push -j1` all green; exact output closure retrievable/substituted from Attic with effective trusted key and signature checks; per-target receipts retained. Route source-free runner materialization failures through existing classification rather than weakening package checks.

Hosted post-land receipt at b3f421e: run 30763888128. x86_64-linux job 91539120302 and aarch64-linux job 91539120362 both passed the pinned closurePublisher shell, then failed closed in Validate publisher and target execution because nix store ping --json did not report trusted=1|true. Exact error: closure publisher must be a trusted Nix store client before restricted cache credentials and signing keys. Attic login/build/version/push/rehydration were all skipped; no cache log artifact directory was created. Darwin jobs 91539120375 and 91539120378 were pending at observation. Classified source-free runner trust materialization; no bypass or source rollback.

title: [broken-on-main] CI dispatches no jobs at all: an unschedulable macOS job deadlocks the concurrency group
description:
Since bd-8dab81 landed at `912159f`, CI has produced no verdict at all. Every run since is `jobs=0` — not a failure, not a cancellation of finished work, but no jobs dispatched whatsoever — and each run is cancelled at the moment the next push creates its successor:

    30431532597  dee8c75  created 07:24:24  cancelled 08:07:42  jobs=0
    30434266559  67e7a6b  created 08:07:41  cancelled 09:00:57  jobs=0
    30437853440  00e30eb  created 09:00:55  cancelled 09:34:28  jobs=0
    30440180776  630c40b  created 09:34:26  pending           jobs=0

The last run that actually reported was 30423738641 at `75fed78`, immediately before the change.

Cause, and it is mine. `bd-8dab81` scoped `cancel-in-progress` to pull requests so a later landing could not kill the slowest job mid-run. What that measurement missed is that **there is no macOS runner registered**: all eight self-hosted runners carry `self-hosted, Linux, X64, nix, x86_64-linux`, and none carries `macos`. The `Nix (macOS)` job requires `[self-hosted, macos]`, so it can never be assigned and its run can never complete.

With cancellation on, that did not matter much: the next push cancelled the stuck run, and the Linux, Node and browser jobs had already dispatched and reported. With cancellation off, the workflow-level concurrency group holds every new run behind the previous one, which never completes, so no jobs dispatch at all. GitHub still replaces a *pending* run when a newer one arrives — only one run may be pending per group — which is why each is cancelled on the next push while never having run anything.

So the change traded "the slowest job rarely reports" for "nothing reports", and the underlying fact it should have established first is that the macOS job has not been runnable at all, making the earlier 6-successes-in-30 measurement a record of a runner that has since gone away.

Fix direction, in preference order:

1. Move the macOS job into its own workflow with its own concurrency group, so a job that cannot be scheduled cannot block the jobs that can. This keeps the original goal — macOS keeps its verdict rather than being cancelled — without coupling it to the fast lane.
2. Restore `cancel-in-progress: true` on the main workflow as the immediate unblock, since a fast lane that reports beats a slow lane that deadlocks.
3. Decide separately whether the macOS job should exist while no macOS runner is registered. A job that cannot be assigned is not coverage, and pretending otherwise is what allowed this to be measured as flakiness rather than absence.

Priority is P1: the repository currently has no working CI, and every landing since 07:24 is unverified.

title: Make recovery-deadline and bootstrap-socket waits load-proof in the standard gate
description:
Two remaining standard-suite gates still race ambient host load, in the same family as bd-41f3d2 and bd-62ea39 but not covered by them.

1. `test/durability.test.mjs` "session recovery open is deadline bounded and records degraded health" runs `mux.recover({ openTimeoutMs: 10, totalOpenTimeoutMs: 20 })` and then asserts the failure code is exactly `recovery_open_timeout`. Those two bounds are 10ms apart, so under contention the total deadline pre-empts the per-open timeout and the truthful bounded outcome `recovery_deadline_exceeded` fails the assertion. The test also asserts `Date.now() - started < 500`, a wall-clock bound inside the deterministic gate.

2. `test/bootstrap-cli.test.mjs` `waitForSocket` fails after a fixed 10 seconds. On a loaded builder the daemon is simply descheduled, producing "daemon did not create its socket within 10 seconds" for a correct binary.

Both reproduced on `nix flake check` at main 4ffa95f with host load average ~15 and again in the standard suite; a rerun of the same tree passed 435/435, which is the signature of load sensitivity rather than a regression.

Fix by making each bounded path deterministic instead of racing: assert the per-open timeout with a total deadline far larger than it, assert the total deadline separately with a per-open timeout far larger than it, and replace tight wall-clock waits with generous hang bounds that still fail a genuinely hung daemon fast via the existing early child-exit check. Do not weaken which codes are considered truthful, and do not drop the degraded-health or non-disclosure assertions.

title: test/tls-fixture.mjs depends on an openssl binary the Node CI lane does not provide
description:
`test/tls-fixture.mjs:12` shells out to the `openssl` binary via `execFile` to generate a self-signed pair, and `test/dashboard-server.test.mjs` and `test/dashboard-dedicated-cli.test.mjs` both depend on it. The binary is an undeclared environmental assumption.

The Nix package build declares it: `flake.nix` lists `pkgs.openssl` in `nativeBuildInputs`, so `nix flake check` has it on PATH. The Node CI job does not: it runs `actions/setup-node` plus `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and `npm test`, with no Nix shell, so it gets whatever the runner image happens to provide. When that is nothing, the tests fail with a bare `ENOENT` naming a spawn failure rather than a missing dependency, which reads like a product fault.

Reported failing tonight by another agent on this project; confirmed by inspection here. It is present on this developer host only via `~/.nix-profile/bin/openssl`, which is exactly the kind of accidental availability that hides the assumption locally.

This is the same class as a browser-launching case sitting in the `test/*.test.mjs` glob (see `bd-2f13cb`, which renamed `test/dash-e2e-nix.test.mjs` and gave it an explicit browser-free invariant): a test whose environmental assumptions hold locally and in one CI lane but not in the lane that actually runs it. The project now has three lanes with materially different environments — the Node job on `setup-node`, the Nix job inside the flake, and the browser smoke job inside `devShells.e2e` — so an undeclared binary dependency is no longer a theoretical problem.

Candidate fixes, in rough order of preference:

1. Generate the pair in-process with `node:crypto` and drop the subprocess entirely. Node can produce a self-signed certificate without shelling out, which removes the dependency rather than declaring it, and makes the fixture faster and platform-independent.
2. Declare and check it: fail early with an explicit message naming `openssl` and the lane that lacks it, so the failure is self-describing rather than an `ENOENT` on spawn.
3. Provide it in the Node CI lane, which fixes CI but leaves a contributor on a machine without `openssl` hitting the same opaque failure.

Whichever is chosen, the fixture should not fail with an unexplained spawn error. Worth a general sweep for other subprocess dependencies in `test/` at the same time.


## Addendum (merged from duplicate bd-13ee48, closed)

Exact failing set observed in CI, both Node jobs (22.19.0 and 24), present since at least d93900d:

    Error: spawn openssl ENOENT
    test/dashboard-dedicated-cli.test.mjs:62  dedicated web CLI authenticates remotely and serves only browser credentials
    test/dashboard-identity-config.test.mjs:79  provider documents and credential sources fail closed
    test/dashboard-server.test.mjs:314  loads bounded owner-controlled TLS file and descriptor sources
    (+2 further TLS cases: native HTTPS SNI/HSTS/downgrade authority, file-backed TLS rotation)

Note `test/dashboard-identity-config.test.mjs` is a third dependent beyond the two named above.

Do not fix this by skipping when openssl is absent. These are the TLS and credential fail-closed cases; a skip would turn the gate green while the security coverage silently disappears, which is worse than the current honest red.

Correction on candidate fix 1, verified rather than assumed: `node:crypto` cannot issue an X.509 certificate. Its `X509Certificate` is parse-only with no static constructor, and `Certificate` is SPKAC handling, not certificate issuance (checked on Node v26.2.0: `X509Certificate` exposes no static creation methods). So "generate the pair in-process with node:crypto" is not reachable through a built-in API — it requires hand-rolled ASN.1/DER TBSCertificate construction, or a new pinned dev dependency. Both are heavier than the problem, so the preference order likely inverts: an explicit `OPENSSL_BIN` override plus providing openssl in the Node lane keeps the matrix and the coverage intact at far lower cost, with fix 2's early self-describing check layered on top.

Also red in the same CI runs: the `Nix (macOS)` job, with a signature nobody has read yet. Worth checking while in here, but it is a separate failure from this one.

title: Assert the property, not that a particular call appears in another file
description:
While applying the negative-control convention I removed an assertion I had
written myself two hours earlier, in `test/tls-fixture-contract.test.mjs`:

    assert.match(identity, /chmod\(secretPath, 0o644\)/);
    assert.match(bootstrap, /chmod\(paths\.stateDir, 0o755\)/);

Moving those fixtures onto a helper broke it, exactly as the formatter break and
the `e2e:nix` string break did earlier the same night. That is the third
instance of the same coupling in one session, and this time I wrote both sides
knowing about the class.

The pattern across all three: an assertion reaches into another file's source
text to check that a particular *implementation* is present, when what it means
is that a *property* holds. `chmod` being called is not the property; the file
being group-readable is. The property was in fact checkable directly — that is
what the helper now does — and asserting it directly is both stronger and
immune to refactoring.

This is adjacent to bd-dff2d8 but not the same bead. That one is about layout
and formatting churn breaking exact-string matches. This is about the choice to
assert an implementation detail in the first place, where a direct check on the
property was available.

Suggested shape: a line in the CONTRIBUTING testing guidance — before asserting
that source text contains a call, ask whether the effect of that call can be
observed directly, and prefer observing it. Keep source-text assertions for
genuinely unobservable structure such as CI wiring, which is where this
repository legitimately uses them.

title: Record the CI concurrency and per-platform budget trade-offs where a workflow editor will see them
description:
bd-8dab81 changed a workflow-level trade-off that the next person to touch `.github/workflows/ci.yml` will hit, and it is currently recorded only in a commit message and a chat exchange.

The trade: cancellation is now scoped to pull requests, so pushes to `main` queue rather than collapsing to the newest. That is deliberate — with unconditional cancellation the slowest job (Nix on macOS) was cancelled on 14 of 30 runs, so a productive night actively eroded its coverage. The cost is that a burst of landings serialises on the single macOS runner and can leave it several commits behind.

The failure mode matters more than the setting: it is self-reinforcing. The faster the project lands, the less often the slowest job is allowed to report, so the coverage degrades exactly when the project is most active — which is also when it is least likely to be noticed, because everything else is green.

What should be written down, briefly, where a workflow editor will see it:

1. Why cancellation is pull-request-only, so nobody "fixes" the queueing by re-enabling it and silently restores the erosion.
2. That the correct response to macOS falling behind is to move it off per-push (schedule or on-demand), not to re-enable cancellation.
3. That per-platform step and job budgets are deliberate: Linux needing more than its budget indicates a real problem, while macOS measured 1.2 to 13.3 minutes on success and needs headroom for a cold cache.

`CONTRIBUTING.md` is the likely home, next to the existing note about wall-clock budgets being opt-in, since both are the same kind of rule: a gate is only worth having if it can actually answer.

title: Acceptances never attach, so neither proves the event half of the consumer path
description:
bd-c4314e found that the integration guide's consumer example received no events at all: it registered a `client.subscribe` listener and never sent `attach`, and event delivery is explicit by design. The same blind spot is in the acceptances.

`test/consumer-acceptance.test.mjs` opens, checks status, and closes, but never attaches, so it proves the request/response half of the consumer path and nothing about the event half. `scripts/live-wake-process-smoke.mjs` performs four real turns and ignores events entirely, so it would pass unchanged against a daemon that delivered none.

Measured here: after `open` and `attach`, zero events arrive without a turn, so the credential-free gate cannot assert delivery. The split follows from that.

- credential-free acceptance: exercise `attach` as part of the documented sequence, so a regression in the sequence a client actually follows fails in the standard gate
- credentialed wake smoke: attach both sessions and assert events actually arrive across the real turns, which is the assertion that would catch a silent consumer

The failure this closes is the dangerous shape: a consumer that opens and wakes without attaching is silent, and the silence is indistinguishable from a model that produced no output.
