title: Correct homepage: configured sessions already support trusted Pi tools and bash
description:
Harry identified that the GitHub Pages homepage says Pi Daemon provides only protocol-v1 no-tools plus the protocol-v2 six-operation filesystem adapter and "still provides no shell or arbitrary extension authority." That is accurate only for the legacy Unix v1 open path and the separate host-adapter capability; as a summary of Pi Daemon today it is materially misleading.

Current main 80d569334dffd95579f87c1efe4ddb2c62651385 already implements authenticated configured sessions through typed SessionSpec: stable cwd, per-session SessionManager/SettingsManager/ResourceLoader, tool modes default/none/no-builtin/allowlist/exclude, Pi built-ins including bash, explicit trusted extension/skill/prompt/theme paths, optional already-installed Pi packages, extension flags, settings, and a memory-only provider/bash environment overlay. Pi RPC exposes arbitrary prompt turns and the stock bash/abort_bash commands when host/session policy enables them. The configured runtime is `unisolated`: it shares the daemon process trust domain, so arbitrary extensions are operator-trusted rather than sandboxed. Built-in bash spawns a bounded child per call; it is not a documented persistent shell. The separate v2 host adapter remains intentionally limited to six cwd-rooted filesystem operations, with parallel reads/searches and sequential writes/edits.

Update `docs/index.md` prominently to distinguish all three surfaces: (1) legacy Unix protocol v1 no-tools compatibility path; (2) authenticated Session API configured sessions with cwd, trusted Pi resources/tools/bash and ordinary agent turns; (3) narrow v2 host filesystem adapter with no shell. Also correct stale/misleading top-level wording in README.md and SECURITY.md if needed while preserving the real default-no-tools and shared-process security boundary. Do not claim persistent shell semantics or guaranteed parallel arbitrary bash commands; document stable cwd and bounded parallel adapter reads accurately. Add a small release/docs contract assertion so the Pages homepage cannot regress to implying all sessions are no-tools. Keep product behavior unchanged.

This is docs-only and should not block or duplicate bd-84e4de physical validation. Hosted required CI owns final validation; run only focused docs/source tests and diff checks locally.

title: Enforce that CI smoke scenarios stay free of numeric tolerances

I added a structural test asserting the wiring exists and that at least three scenarios carry the tag, which prevents the empty-selection failure mode, but it cannot assert the more interesting property: that every tagged scenario is actually load-proof. A scenario could acquire a wall-clock or pixel tolerance later and quietly become a flaky gate. Consider a check that rejects a `@smoke` scenario whose body contains a bare numeric tolerance comparison (a `toBeLessThan`/`toBeGreaterThan` against a literal that is not routed through `reportPerformanceBudget`), so the subset's defining property — structure only, no timing or pixel bounds — is enforced rather than remembered. title: Nix (macOS) answers on one run in five: timeouts and concurrency cancellations
description:
Measured across the last 30 CI runs, the `Nix (macOS)` job concluded:

    success    6
    failure    7
    cancelled 14
    queued     3

So it answers on about one run in five, and is cancelled on nearly half. Two
separate mechanisms produce that, and neither is a product fault.

**Cancellations.** The workflow sets `cancel-in-progress: true` on a
`ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` group. macOS is by far the slowest
job, so a subsequent push to `main` — routine with several agents landing —
cancels it while the Linux and Node jobs have already finished. The faster the
project lands, the less often macOS is allowed to report.

**Timeouts.** The 7 failures are not test failures. Sampling job 90442980837
(run 30409736168), the suite inside the check reports `ℹ fail 0` and the job
ends with:

    ##[error]The action 'Run nix flake check --print-build-logs' has timed out after 25 minutes.

Successful macOS runs took 1.2, 1.2, 2.6, 9.7, 9.8 and 13.3 minutes, so the
spread is wide and the 25-minute ceiling is close enough to the slow tail to be
hit whenever the runner has to build rather than substitute. The same shape
already bit the formatter check I added, which timed out on macOS at 5 minutes
while passing on Linux, and was fixed by pinning it to one platform (`cda4137`,
repaired in `ad33e87`).

Worth deciding deliberately, because the current state is the worst of both: the
job costs runner time on most pushes and rarely produces a verdict, so nobody
reads it and a genuine macOS regression would be indistinguishable from the
usual noise. Options, not mutually exclusive:

1. Give macOS a longer step budget, and possibly the whole job, so a cold cache
   can finish.
2. Exclude macOS from `cancel-in-progress`, or move it to its own concurrency
   group, so a later push does not kill a run that was going to answer.
3. Run macOS on a schedule or on demand rather than per push, accepting slower
   feedback in exchange for a verdict that is actually read.
4. Investigate why the spread is 1.2 to 13.3 minutes — a cache that is
   populated on some runs and not others is the likely cause, and fixing that
   may remove the problem rather than accommodate it.

Filed from the bd-7cba4b session, which noted the macOS job was red with a
signature nobody had read. This is that signature.
creator: sonance:pi-daemon:sonance-pi-daemon-pidm-pico-on-demand-dev-test-son

title: Give the web unit suite a DOM environment so component regressions are testable in the standard gate
description:
`web/vite.config.ts` declares no vitest `environment`, so the web unit suite
runs in plain Node with no DOM. That is fine for pure logic, and the existing
`chat-pane-layout.test.ts` works around it by testing exported pure functions
and by string-matching component source with `readFile`.

The cost shows up on any bug that lives in DOM/layout behaviour. While fixing
bd-94d7df (transcript reading position across a Rich/TUI switch) the entire
regression surface -- ResizeObserver transitions, hidden-layer relayout,
virtualizer remeasurement, scroll restoration -- was only reachable through the
Playwright suite, which CI never runs. The landed unit tests cover the extracted
anchor arithmetic, which is real but is the easy half; the part that actually
broke could not be unit-tested at all.

The source-string assertions are a symptom of the same gap: asserting
`expect(source).toContain("useVirtualizer")` is a proxy for behaviour that a DOM
environment could assert directly.

Suggested shape: add a jsdom or happy-dom vitest environment for the web
workspace so component-level regressions of this class get a deterministic test
that runs in the standard gate, rather than depending on a browser suite that CI
skips. Scope it deliberately -- this is not a request to port the Playwright
suite, only to make DOM-level unit tests possible.

title: Explain the macOS Nix job's order-of-magnitude runtime spread
description:
bd-8dab81 accommodated the macOS Nix job's runtime spread by raising its budgets; it did not explain the spread. Successful runs measured 1.2, 1.2, 2.6, 9.7, 9.8 and 13.3 minutes for the same `nix flake check` on the same runner class. An order of magnitude between fastest and slowest suggests some runs substitute from a cache and others build from source, rather than genuine variance in the work.

Worth establishing, in rough order of cheapness:

1. Whether the macOS runner has a binary cache configured at all beyond `cache.nixos.org`, and whether the project's own derivations (the package, the pages build, the home-manager module check) are ever substitutable there. If nothing publishes them, every eviction means a from-source rebuild and the fast runs are simply the ones that hit a warm local store.
2. Whether the local store is being garbage-collected between runs, which would explain warm and cold runs alternating without any configuration change.
3. Whether the slow runs correlate with a specific derivation. `--print-build-logs` is already on, so a slow run's log should name what it built; comparing a 1.2-minute log against a 13.3-minute one would settle it in one reading.

If the cause is a missing binary cache for project derivations, fixing it removes the problem rather than budgeting around it, and would also shorten the Linux lane. If it is garbage collection, the budget raise is the correct permanent answer and this bead can be closed as explained.

Filed via reflect-session mixin from the bd-8dab81 session.


## Correction (bd-775c57): the premise no longer holds

The measurements above are real but they describe a runner that is no longer registered. `gh api repos/harryaskham/pi-daemon/actions/runners` lists eight self-hosted runners, all carrying `self-hosted, Linux, X64, nix, x86_64-linux`; none carries `macos`. The `Nix (macOS)` job therefore cannot be assigned at all, which is why it never reports, and the 1.2 to 13.3 minute spread is a record of a machine that has since gone away.

So this bead should not be worked as written. Comparing a fast run's build log against a slow one is not possible while no run happens, and a cache hypothesis cannot be tested against a runner that does not exist.

What is still worth doing, in order:

1. Decide whether a macOS runner should be registered again, which is an operator question rather than a repository one. The job now lives in its own workflow (`ci-macos.yml`, bd-775c57) where it queues harmlessly, so nothing is blocked while that is decided.
2. If one is registered, re-measure before assuming the old spread still describes it — a different machine will have a different cache and a different tail.
3. Only then investigate the spread, if it recurs.

Recorded rather than closed, because the underlying question — whether project derivations are substitutable on macOS or rebuilt every time — remains a real one that would shorten the Linux lane too if the answer is a missing binary cache.

title: Capability-gate supervisord stopwaitsecs for Nix-on-Droid schemas
description:
Nix-on-Droid evaluation fails because Pi Daemon's Home Manager module unconditionally emits `supervisord.programs.<service>.stopwaitsecs`, but the active typed schema from collective-public/modules/supervisord-program-options.nix does not define that option and its config renderer does not output it. The Pi Daemon module check masks the mismatch by stubbing `supervisord.programs` as attrsOf anything, and even asserts the unsupported field.

Fix Pi Daemon compatibility now: introspect the imported supervisord programs element suboptions and include stopwaitsecs only when supported. Keep command, environment, autorestart, startsecs, stopsignal and log options unchanged. Replace permissive test stub with a strict schema matching current Nix-on-Droid options; prove evaluation succeeds and stopwaitsecs is absent. Add a second schema that exposes stopwaitsecs and prove Pi Daemon emits the rounded graceful timeout there, preserving forward compatibility when Collective gains support. Document fallback to supervisor's own default when the schema lacks the option.

Separately route an upstream Collective improvement to add typed stopwaitsecs and render it, so configured gracefulTimeoutMs can eventually carry through on Nix-on-Droid. Pi Daemon must not require that rollout to evaluate.

title: Hermeticize pi-daemon npm-deps staging against registry HTTP/2 fetch failures
description:
## Trigger

Authenticated one-shot Cacophony Android Play-test release failed closed while building the Pi Daemon dependency.

Exact receipt:

- first-party job `rj-4e1e52e3`
- provider run `30776334395`
- source `f53fa8084ee984754765c3cd0fcb0b96402de6a9`
- versionName `1.2.1594`
- expected phone versionCode `19894`, Wear `1019894`
- failed at `2026-08-03T02:52:22Z`

JVM tests and signing-key materialization passed. Native staging failed building `pi-daemon-0.3.0-npm-deps` because `registry.npmjs.org` returned HTTP/2 framing error `[92]` while fetching:

    lightningcss-linux-arm64-gnu-1.32.0.tgz

APK/AAB/provenance/e2e and every upload/promotion step were skipped. Provider artifact count 0. No Play credentials, receipt, upload, or track mutation. Existing tester baseline unchanged. Retry authority was one-shot and is exhausted.

## Problem

A fixed, lockfile-pinned Pi Daemon npm dependency build can fail an unrelated Android release because native staging still depends on a live npm registry tarball fetch. One transient HTTP/2 framing failure aborts the complete signed release pipeline after earlier guards pass.

## Required behavior

Make the Pi Daemon npm-deps staging path hermetic or boundedly resilient without weakening package integrity:

- prefer pinned/vendor/cache materialization for lockfile-resolved tarballs
- if network remains necessary, bounded retry/backoff must distinguish transient transport from integrity failure
- verify exact package name/version/hash; never bypass npm integrity checks
- preserve fail-closed behavior for checksum, package identity, or signing failures
- surface a typed infrastructure receipt naming dependency, transport class, attempts, and cleanup

## Acceptance

- regression fixture injects HTTP/2/transient fetch failure for `lightningcss-linux-arm64-gnu-1.32.0.tgz`
- staging succeeds from hermetic cache/vendor input OR bounded retry recovers without duplicate side effects
- integrity mismatch still fails immediately and clearly
- Cacophony Android native staging can build `pi-daemon-0.3.0-npm-deps` without ambient registry availability once inputs are cached
- no tokens, npm credentials, Play credentials, signing material, or registry auth leak into logs
- after landing/deployment, Android release owner obtains new explicit retry authority; the exhausted run above is never reused

## Dedupe

Searches across both `cacophony` and `pi-daemon` for the package name, HTTP/2 framing error, and npm-deps found no matching bead.
creator: helsinki:pi-daemon:helsinki-cacophony-cluster-ctrl

title: Dash Rich/TUI presentation switch does not restore transcript reading position
description:
Discovered while landing bd-185516 (Nix Playwright shell), on NixOS with the audited nixpkgs browser bundle.

The e2e assertion at web/e2e/dash.spec.ts (test "TUI presentation streams one canonical controller grid to read-only pane mirrors") reads `.transcript` scrollTop immediately after `page.goto`, switches Rich -> TUI -> Rich, reads it again, and asserts the two are within 200px. On an idle host both reads happen before ChatPane's autoscroll effect runs, so both are ~0 and the assertion proves nothing. Under host load the second read lands after the autoscroll and the test fails with ~1400px, which is how it was found.

Measured with settled reads (wait for a rendered [data-transcript-row], then require three consecutive stable samples), repeated three times deterministically:

- distance from bottom before the switch: 111px
- distance from bottom after returning to Rich: 2510px

So the reading position is NOT restored across a presentation switch: the pane lands roughly 2.5k px above where it was. Absolute scrollTop is also not comparable across remounts, because @tanstack/react-virtual dynamic measurement changes the total size (24329 vs 22658 for the same "pinned to last record" state); distance from the bottom is the stable quantity.

Two separable pieces of work:

1. Decide the intended behaviour for Rich -> TUI -> Rich. Either genuinely restore the previous reading position, or define "returns to the latest record" as the contract.
2. Rewrite the assertion against settled distance-from-bottom so it actually tests that contract instead of comparing two pre-hydration zeros.

Note that repository CI runs the Node suite and `nix flake check` but never the browser suite, so browser regressions of this shape only surface in a local `just dash-e2e` run.

title: Detect and repair pid-healthy but HTTP-dead Dash services
description:
The Home Manager `daemon-main` API and web processes can remain pid/listener-healthy while returning no HTTP bytes indefinitely. This leaves Dash dead but launchd sees both jobs as running and never repairs them.

INCIDENT 2026-08-01, ordinary daemon-main only (Cacophony-owned instance was separate and unaffected):
- API PID60662 and web PID62145 had run for ~3 days and both listened on 127.0.0.1:7463/7465
- curl connected but received no response before 5-10s bounds; /dash was unusable
- both processes showed 0 CPU and no new readiness/fatal log entry
- web ignored SIGTERM for 30s and retained PID/listener state; required job-local `launchctl kickstart -k`
- API daemon accepted SIGTERM and emitted host_draining at 2026-08-01T23:18:14Z; launchd replaced it with PID62123
- under host pressure, daemon did not bind/ready until 23:21:11Z (~177s), host instance 4f9d50bd, zero retained/recovery failures
- web initially saw remote_unavailable, then launchd replacement PID68897 emitted web_ready at 23:22:58Z
- post-repair: /dash HTTP200 in 0.366s; API root expected HTTP401 in 0.040s
- Cacophony-owned PID65432/socket was not touched and remained running

HOST CONDITIONS (important reproducer, not an excuse to report healthy): root filesystem 922/927GB used, only 5.4GB available (100% in df display); load ~60-76; stock Pi sessions 4.3GB. The replacement eventually recovered without deleting data once load progressed.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. service health must distinguish pid/listener existence from bounded HTTP/API responsiveness;
2. a wedged component gets a bounded, instance-scoped recovery that never touches another Pi Daemon instance;
3. recovery preserves graceful drain where it works, but has an audited bounded escalation for an event loop that cannot process SIGTERM;
4. startup/readiness diagnostics expose the stage responsible for multi-minute delay instead of showing only a running PID;
5. supervision must not form a restart storm under disk/load pressure; one recovery attempt plus explicit degraded state is preferable;
6. tests cover TCP-accepting/no-response and a web process waiting on an unavailable API.

2026-08-02 RECURRENCE WITHOUT RESTART: initial bounded probes to both daemon-main API and Dash received no bytes before 5s, on the replacement PIDs62123/68897. Three immediate API retries then returned expected401 with latency 4.342s, 3.318s, 2.984s; web returned200 in 1.928s, 0.555s, 0.573s. Host load was 51.91/53.91/47.13. No lifecycle action was taken because semantic responses recovered. A 2-second native sample of daemon main thread showed 1423/1424 samples under libuv work completion -> node fs AfterInteger callback, while web was largely normal kevent/stream IO. This points at filesystem/inventory pressure starving request latency rather than dead TCP accept. Acceptance should cover degraded-latency reporting and request isolation under long inventory filesystem work, not only total no-response.

title: shutdown-deadline test fails under host load
description:
`serve shutdown honors one whole deadline when adapter disposal hangs` (test/server.test.mjs) fails under host load on unchanged code.

The test proves shutdown is BOUNDED when an adapter's dispose() hangs. It does that two ways: it asserts an `adapter_dispose_timeout`/`host_shutdown_timeout` event was emitted, which is the real semantic check, and it also asserts `Date.now() - started < 1_000`. That second assertion is a tight wall-clock proxy spanning CLI startup, socket bind, a client connect, an open request, and process teardown, so it measures host scheduling as much as the shutdown bound.

Observed on an otherwise healthy tree at load average ~32-39: 1586ms against the 1000ms bound, failing the standard gate. Same failure mode as bd-41f3d2/bd-62ea39/bd-79902f: a fixed millisecond bound encoding an assumption about how fast a healthy machine is.

Fix: keep the timeout-event assertion as the semantic proof and replace the tight proxy with a generous hang bound that still fails a genuinely unbounded shutdown, exactly as bd-79902f did for the bootstrap socket wait. Do not weaken the event assertion.

title: status does not report the model a session is bound to
description:
Neither `status` nor any response names the model a session is actually bound to. Recovering it currently requires scanning the event stream, which is how the substitution in bd-d18fe2 was identified at all, and is not something a consumer should have to do.

The value depends on how bd-d18fe2 is decided, and it is worth doing either way:

- if unknown models are refused at open, the bound model always equals the named one, and reporting it is confirmation rather than detection
- if substitution stays, reporting it is the only way a client can tell it happened

It also makes the chosen fix verifiable. With the bound model observable, the wake harness can assert it equals what the client named, so whichever semantics land can be proven rather than inspected.

Implementation sketch, from reading the seam:

- `src/pi-adapter.ts` already computes the bound model in `model` before `#createSession`, at the end of the resolution chain `resolvedModel ?? legacyModel ?? scopedModels[0] ?? getAvailable()[0]`
- it is not returned to the caller, so `SessionSlot` in `src/multiplexer.ts` cannot store it and `snapshot()` at multiplexer.ts:2380 cannot report it
- `SessionSnapshot` (multiplexer.ts:121) would gain an optional `model: { provider, id }`, following the existing optional-field pattern used by `activeRequestId` and `lastErrorCode`

Protocol surface change, so per AGENTS.md it needs schema updates, fixtures, and compatibility coverage, not just the plumbing.

Sequenced deliberately after bd-d18fe2: starting it before the semantics are decided risks building observability for behaviour that is about to change.

title: 41 owner-mismatch guards on credential and config paths, none exercised by a test
description:
Verified rather than assumed, following the uid axis discussion on bd-b6c8cb.

There are 41 owner-mismatch guards of the shape `info.uid !== getuid()` across 21
source files — the identity provider, the config loader, the API bearer loader,
the auth seed, the dashboard credential and descriptor loaders, and the
authorization store. Searching the test suite for the errors they raise finds
nothing:

    "must be owned by the current user"   0 tests
    "owned by current user"               0 tests
    identity_provider_owner_mismatch      0 tests

So no test exercises any of them. That is a structural gap rather than an
oversight: every fixture is created by the process that then loads it, so
`info.uid` always equals `getuid()` and the guard is unreachable by construction.

The part worth correcting in bd-b6c8cb: this is *not* reachable by a variation
lane either. Running the suite under a different uid does not help, because the
fixtures are created by that same uid — the comparison stays equal. Running as
root does not help for the same reason. Reaching it needs either privileged
fixture setup, which is not appropriate for the standard gate, or the second
form from the negative-control convention: extract the predicate and check in the
cases it should reject.

The second is cheap and is what the convention already recommends when the
property is not observable end-to-end. A shared `ownsPath(info, uid)` helper, or
equivalent, tested directly against the mismatch cases would cover all 41 sites'
logic once, without any fixture needing a foreign owner.

Scope to decide before implementing:

- whether the 41 sites should share one predicate or keep their local checks with
  a tested helper behind them;
- whether the `info.uid !== 0` root exemption present in some of them and absent
  in others is deliberate — `config.ts` and `dashboard-identity-config.ts` accept
  root-owned files, `api-auth.ts` and `dashboard-auth.ts` do not. That difference
  may be correct, but it is currently unexplained and untested, which is the
  weaker position of the two.

Priority is P2 rather than P3 because these are fail-closed ownership checks on
credential, token, and configuration paths, and none of them is known to work.

Diagnosis posted before anyone starts, since the bead says the root question
should be settled first and it changes what tests are worth writing.

The inconsistency is not one: it is a coherent policy that happens to be
undocumented in the code. Grouping the 41 guards by whether they accept
`info.uid === 0`:

Accepts root — configuration and provisioned material:
  config.ts, dashboard-identity-config.ts, dashboard-server.ts,
  dashboard-session-defaults.ts, dashboard-tls.ts,
  installed-package-resources.ts, pi-adapter.ts, schedule-config.ts

Rejects root — secrets the service owns:
  api-auth.ts (bearer token), bootstrap.ts (Pi auth seed),
  dashboard-auth.ts (credential and descriptor), dashboard-authorization.ts
  (authorization store, 7 guards)

The split is material the system provisions for the service versus material the
service holds as its own secret. Root-owned configuration is a normal deployment
— a Nix store path, a system config file, a Home Manager symlink — and this is
already documented policy rather than an accident: `docs/operations.md:186` says
the configuration file "must resolve to a regular current-user/root-owned file
that is not group/world writable". A root-owned bearer token or auth seed is not
a normal deployment of the same kind, and rejecting it is defensible.

`dashboard-tls.ts` is the boundary case and I think it is on the right side. A
private key is secret, but a root-owned key provisioned by a system ACME or PKI
setup is ordinary, and the service must be able to read it. It groups with
provisioned material rather than with the service's own secrets.

So the recommendation is: do not unify the guards. The difference is intended and
the right fix is to make it legible and tested rather than to flatten it — a
predicate taking the policy as a parameter, something like
`ownedBy(info, { allowRoot: true })`, with checked-in cases for both policies,
and the reasoning stated once where the predicate lives.

Worth noting what remains genuinely unverified: I inferred the policy from the
grouping and one line of operations documentation. Nobody has confirmed it was
intended, and the possibility that one of the 41 is on the wrong side of the line
by accident is exactly what no test would currently catch. The predicate should
therefore be introduced per call site deliberately rather than mechanically, so
each site's policy is chosen rather than inherited from whatever it does today.

title: Hydrate exact Attic output non-recursively; recursive copy falsely requires upstream public dependencies
description:
# bd-833b3e — exact-output non-recursive hydration follow-up

## Hosted evidence

Run 30776593976, source 3029b17:
- both Darwin targets: build/version/push success; recursive hydration fails on
  upstream dependencies (Node.js / Bash);
- post-reboot x86 Linux canary: same — push succeeds, hydration fails on upstream
  Bash path;
- Attic push reports `0 already cached, 49/57 in upstream`.

Attic stores the exact pi-daemon output but intentionally does not duplicate
public dependencies already in upstream caches. `nix copy` is recursive by
default, so Attic-only hydration requests paths Attic never stored.

## Patch

- Rename step to exact signed output path hydration.
- Add `--no-recursive` to the signed copy. This proves the exact pushed output
  NAR is present and signed without falsely requiring Attic to own all upstream
  dependencies.
- Correct error/summary wording: exact output path, not full self-contained
  closure; public transitive deps remain signed in upstream caches.
- Acceptance test requires `--no-recursive`.
- Negative mutation removes it and must fail, preventing regression to recursive
  hydration.
- Update ordering assertion to the new exact invocation.

If product acceptance truly requires a self-contained Attic closure, do NOT use
this patch: explicitly change push policy to duplicate all upstream deps instead.
That is a separate product/storage decision.

## Validation

- focused ci-acceptance-boundaries: 2/2 PASS
- actionlint: exit 0
- disposable clone only; no canonical checkout/host mutation

## Exact diff

diff --git a/.github/workflows/closure-cache.yml b/.github/workflows/closure-cache.yml
index a3087c5..f99b3c5 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/closure-cache.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/closure-cache.yml
@@ -198,7 +198,7 @@ jobs:
           # the hydration step so private-read auth cannot pass accidentally.
           rm -rf "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME"
 
-      - name: Hydrate the exact signed closure from Attic
+      - name: Hydrate the exact signed output path from Attic
         shell: bash
         env:
           PACKAGE_OUT: ${{ steps.build.outputs.out }}
@@ -209,7 +209,12 @@ jobs:
           hydration_root="$canonical_runner_temp/attic-hydration-$TARGET_SYSTEM"
           hydration_store="local?root=$hydration_root"
           mkdir -p "$hydration_root"
-          nix copy --option require-sigs true \
+          # bd-833b3e: prove the exact uploaded output NAR, not ownership of
+          # every transitive dependency. Attic intentionally leaves public
+          # dependencies in upstream caches (the push reports them as
+          # "in upstream"), so recursive copy from Attic alone asks it for
+          # paths it never duplicated and fails despite a successful push.
+          nix copy --no-recursive --option require-sigs true \
             --from "$ATTIC_SUBSTITUTER" \
             --to "$hydration_store" \
             "$PACKAGE_OUT" \
@@ -219,7 +224,7 @@ jobs:
             nix path-info --store "$hydration_store" "$PACKAGE_OUT"
           )
           if [[ "$hydrated_out" != "$PACKAGE_OUT" || ! -x "$hydration_root$PACKAGE_OUT/bin/pi-daemon" ]]; then
-            echo '::error title=Attic hydration did not reproduce the exact output::The signed cache must hydrate the captured package into an empty isolated local store.'
+            echo '::error title=Attic hydration did not reproduce the exact output path::The signed cache must hydrate the captured output NAR into an empty isolated local store.'
             exit 1
           fi
           printf '%s\n' "$hydrated_out" > "$log_dir/attic-hydrated-output"
@@ -230,7 +235,7 @@ jobs:
             echo "- cache: \`${ATTIC_CACHE}\`"
             echo "- execution: \`${TARGET_EXECUTION}\` from \`${CURRENT_SYSTEM}\`"
             echo '- verification: both installed version commands executed'
-            echo '- trust: exact output rehydrated from Attic into an empty local store with require-sigs enabled'
+            echo '- trust: exact output path rehydrated non-recursively from Attic into an empty local store with require-sigs enabled; public transitive dependencies remain in signed upstream caches'
           } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
 
       - name: Remove Attic credentials

title: Clarify Pages and README: configured sessions support bash, built-in tools and trusted extensions
description:
docs/index.md currently opens with the accurate but misleading statement that protocol v1 is no-tools and protocol v2 has only six filesystem operations, then immediately lists full service surfaces without stating that authenticated SessionSpec creation already supports Pi-equivalent tool/resource policy. README safety defaults likewise still say no built-in tools/no arbitrary extensions as though that describes the whole current product. Correct the product-level overview while preserving protocol facts: legacy Unix protocol v1 remains no-tools; protocol v2's host adapter remains fixed filesystem-only; authenticated configured sessions can select tools mode default/none/no-builtin/allowlist/exclude, load explicit trusted extension/skill/prompt/theme paths under projectTrust approve, and replace built-in bash with a cwd-bound spawn hook carrying the bounded session env overlay. State the limits honestly: unisolated is one shared JavaScript trust domain; extension pi.exec/process.env remain ambient; each session has one active model turn, global turns are bounded, and bash calls are child invocations rather than a guaranteed persistent shell process. Update docs/index.md, README.md safety/product sections, quickstart/session-configuration links and a source/Pages assertion so future scaffold wording cannot again hide full-host capability. Filed from operator question on 2026-08-06; no implementation claim because reporting worker checkout is under post-squash alignment hold.

---

## Merged duplicate: bd-5afbd0

Title: Clarify GitHub Pages support for configured tools and trusted extensions

The GitHub Pages landing page says Protocol v1 is intentionally no-tools and protocol v2 only exposes six filesystem operations. That is narrowly true for legacy Unix NDJSON v1 and the host-adapter v2 profile, but the placement reads as a product-wide limitation and is now misleading. The authenticated Session API already accepts typed configured sessions with default/none/no-builtin/allowlist tool policies, explicit trusted extensions/skills/prompts/themes, built-in bash scoped to the session cwd/environment hook, and persistent AgentSessionRuntime conversation state. Update the landing page and adjacent overview docs to distinguish legacy UDS/v2 host-adapter restrictions from the full configured Session API. title: Fire every guard introduced tonight and read what it prints
description:
Acting on the generalisation landed with the failure-text convention (`8e4858f`): every guard carries advice that no green run has ever read. Rather than leave that as an observation, I fired each assertion I introduced tonight and read what it prints.

Six of seven were accurate and actionable: the CI job-timeout invariant, the macOS-separation invariant, the smoke-wiring invariant, the ownership census, the SDK-override guard, and the session-dir drift alarm (already corrected under bd-4d813c, which is what prompted this).

One had aged out of truth. The exposure census message read "a mode mask was added, removed, or changed" and advised that "widening from 0o077 to 0o022 is a change of policy, not of formatting". That described the world when it was written. The adoption sweep (bd-568050) then moved nearly every site from an octal literal to a named policy, so the change that now fires it is a `"private"` becoming `"no-foreign-writers"`, and a reader following the message would grep for octal literals and find none — only two remain in the entire source tree.

The assertion stayed correct throughout. Only its advice rotted, and it rotted because of a legitimate refactor of the code it watches, which is a mechanism worth naming: a failure message can be invalidated by a change that leaves the assertion passing, so nothing about that change surfaces the staleness. There is no green run that reads it and no failing run to correct it.

Fixed the message to name both shapes, to say explicitly that chasing octal literals will find nothing, and to state that either direction is a policy change — widening exposes material the site was protecting, narrowing breaks session state that is deliberately readable. Verified by firing it again and reading the corrected text.

Also worth recording: my first attempt at this audit produced a false alarm. I mutated an octal literal in `api-auth.ts` to test the exposure census, the test stayed green, and I briefly concluded my own guard was vacuous. The instrument was wrong — that file no longer contains a literal to mutate, and the census had been correctly updated during adoption to count named policies. Checking the instrument before trusting its disagreement (bd-1cdff9) applied to me within an hour of it being filed.

src/pi-adapter.ts

title: Publish the complete Attic closure; non-recursive root hydration still fails reference validity
description:
# bd-833b3e corrective follow-up — preserve self-contained Attic closure

## Correction

The landed `bd-a287a2` non-recursive hydration fix is wrong. Hosted exact-source
run proves `nix copy --no-recursive` still imports the root NAR and then rejects
it because referenced paths are absent from the empty destination store. Both
Linux jobs fail on Node/Bash dependencies even with `--no-recursive`.

The original acceptance was a **self-contained signed closure**, not only a root
output NAR. Attic's default push says `49/57 in upstream` and omits those paths.
The correct control is Attic's own:

```
attic push --ignore-upstream-cache-filter
```

That publishes every dependency into Attic, after which ordinary recursive
hydration from Attic into an empty local store is the correct proof.

## Patch

- Add `--ignore-upstream-cache-filter` to exact `attic push`.
- Restore recursive `nix copy --option require-sigs true`.
- Restore wording to exact self-contained closure.
- Add negative mutation removing the push flag; boundary test must fail.
- Explicitly assert hydration is not `--no-recursive`.
- Fix cleanup: local-store objects are read-only; `chmod -R u+w ... || true`
  before `rm -rf` prevents the observed cleanup `Permission denied` failures.

## Hosted evidence

Run `30810507444` exact source `5581f40`:

- x86 Linux: build/version/push success, non-rec hydration fails on Bash ref.
- aarch Linux: build/version/push success, non-rec hydration fails on Node.js ref.
- same failure as prior Darwin jobs.

The root output path begins copying from Attic, then Nix enforces reference
validity. This is not a trust/auth/transport failure.

## Validation

Disposable clone of current pi-daemon main:

- focused `ci-acceptance-boundaries`: 2/2 PASS
- actionlint: exit 0
- no host/canonical checkout mutation

## Exact diff

diff --git a/.github/workflows/closure-cache.yml b/.github/workflows/closure-cache.yml
index f99b3c5..d938703 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/closure-cache.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/closure-cache.yml
@@ -192,13 +192,18 @@ jobs:
           nix develop .#closurePublisher --command attic login --set-default pi-daemon-ci "$ATTIC_ENDPOINT" "$ATTIC_TOKEN"
           nix develop .#closurePublisher --command attic cache info "pi-daemon-ci:${ATTIC_CACHE}" \
             | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/attic-cache-info-$TARGET_SYSTEM.log"
-          nix develop .#closurePublisher --command attic push -j1 "pi-daemon-ci:${ATTIC_CACHE}" "$PACKAGE_OUT" \
+          # bd-833b3e: publish the ENTIRE closure. Attic's default upstream
+          # filter omits paths already available from public caches; that is good
+          # for storage efficiency but makes an Attic-only empty-store hydration
+          # impossible. The acceptance contract is a self-contained signed
+          # closure, so deliberately override the filter.
+          nix develop .#closurePublisher --command attic push -j1 --ignore-upstream-cache-filter "pi-daemon-ci:${ATTIC_CACHE}" "$PACKAGE_OUT" \
             2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/closure-cache-$TARGET_SYSTEM/attic-push.log"
           # Public signed reads are host-declared. Remove push credentials before
           # the hydration step so private-read auth cannot pass accidentally.
           rm -rf "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME"
 
-      - name: Hydrate the exact signed output path from Attic
+      - name: Hydrate the exact signed closure from Attic
         shell: bash
         env:
           PACKAGE_OUT: ${{ steps.build.outputs.out }}
@@ -209,12 +214,11 @@ jobs:
           hydration_root="$canonical_runner_temp/attic-hydration-$TARGET_SYSTEM"
           hydration_store="local?root=$hydration_root"
           mkdir -p "$hydration_root"
-          # bd-833b3e: prove the exact uploaded output NAR, not ownership of
-          # every transitive dependency. Attic intentionally leaves public
-          # dependencies in upstream caches (the push reports them as
-          # "in upstream"), so recursive copy from Attic alone asks it for
-          # paths it never duplicated and fails despite a successful push.
-          nix copy --no-recursive --option require-sigs true \
+          # bd-833b3e: recursive copy is intentional. The preceding push uses
+          # --ignore-upstream-cache-filter so Attic must own every reference of
+          # the exact output; empty-store hydration proves the self-contained
+          # signed closure rather than only the root NAR.
+          nix copy --option require-sigs true \
             --from "$ATTIC_SUBSTITUTER" \
             --to "$hydration_store" \
             "$PACKAGE_OUT" \
@@ -224,7 +228,7 @@ jobs:
             nix path-info --store "$hydration_store" "$PACKAGE_OUT"
           )
           if [[ "$hydrated_out" != "$PACKAGE_OUT" || ! -x "$hydration_root$PACKAGE_OUT/bin/pi-daemon" ]]; then
-            echo '::error title=Attic hydration did not reproduce the exact output path::The signed cache must hydrate the captured output NAR into an empty isolated local store.'
+            echo '::error title=Attic hydration did not reproduce the exact output closure::The signed cache must hydrate the captured package and every reference into an empty isolated local store.'
             exit 1
           fi
           printf '%s\n' "$hydrated_out" > "$log_dir/attic-hydrated-output"
@@ -235,13 +239,16 @@ jobs:
             echo "- cache: \`${ATTIC_CACHE}\`"
             echo "- execution: \`${TARGET_EXECUTION}\` from \`${CURRENT_SYSTEM}\`"
             echo '- verification: both installed version commands executed'
-            echo '- trust: exact output path rehydrated non-recursively from Attic into an empty local store with require-sigs enabled; public transitive dependencies remain in signed upstream caches'
+            echo '- trust: exact self-contained closure rehydrated recursively from Attic into an empty local store with require-sigs enabled'
           } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
 
       - name: Remove Attic credentials
         if: always()
         shell: bash
         run: |
+          # Nix local-store objects are read-only; restore owner write bits so
+          # cleanup does not fail with Permission denied after hydration errors.
+          chmod -R u+w "$RUNNER_TEMP/attic-hydration-$TARGET_SYSTEM" 2>/dev/null || true
           rm -rf "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME" "$RUNNER_TEMP/attic-hydration-$TARGET_SYSTEM"
           rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/nix-config-before-attic-$TARGET_SYSTEM.json" \
             "$RUNNER_TEMP/nix-store-trust-$TARGET_SYSTEM.json" \
diff --git a/test/ci-acceptance-boundaries.test.mjs b/test/ci-acceptance-boundaries.test.mjs
index d62fdde..c8676cf 100644

-  assert.match(closure, /nix develop \.#closurePublisher --command attic push -j1 "pi-daemon-ci:\$\{ATTIC_CACHE\}" "\$PACKAGE_OUT"/);
-  assert.match(closure, /nix copy --no-recursive --option require-sigs true/);
+  assert.match(closure, /nix develop \.#closurePublisher --command attic push -j1 --ignore-upstream-cache-filter "pi-daemon-ci:\$\{ATTIC_CACHE\}" "\$PACKAGE_OUT"/);
+  assert.match(closure, /nix copy --option require-sigs true/);
+  assert.doesNotMatch(closure, /nix copy --no-recursive/);
   assert.match(closure, /--from "\$ATTIC_SUBSTITUTER"/);
   assert.match(closure, /--to "\$hydration_store"/);
   assert.match(closure, /canonical_runner_temp="\$\(cd "\$RUNNER_TEMP" && pwd -P\)"/);
@@ -117,9 +118,9 @@ function assertAcceptanceBoundaries({ manifest, flake, ci, macos, scheduled, clo
   const trustBoundary = closure.indexOf("shared github-runner principal is unexpectedly a trusted Nix client");
   const build = closure.indexOf('".#packages.${TARGET_SYSTEM}.pi-daemon"');
   const login = closure.indexOf("nix develop .#closurePublisher --command attic login --set-default");
-  const push = closure.indexOf('nix develop .#closurePublisher --command attic push -j1 "pi-daemon-ci:${ATTIC_CACHE}" "$PACKAGE_OUT"');
+  const push = closure.indexOf('nix develop .#closurePublisher --command attic push -j1 --ignore-upstream-cache-filter "pi-daemon-ci:${ATTIC_CACHE}" "$PACKAGE_OUT"');
   const credentialRemoval = closure.indexOf('rm -rf "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME"', push);
-  const hydrate = closure.indexOf("nix copy --no-recursive --option require-sigs true");
+  const hydrate = closure.indexOf("nix copy --option require-sigs true");
   assert.ok(trustBoundary < build && build < login && login < push && push < credentialRemoval && credentialRemoval < hydrate, "untrusted-client proof and exact build must precede push-only credentials, cleanup, and signed hydration");
 }
 
@@ -242,10 +243,10 @@ test("CI boundary checks reject regressions in every asserted direction", async
       },

     {
-      name: "publisher restores recursive hydration and demands upstream dependencies from Attic",
+      name: "publisher restores Attic upstream filtering and loses the self-contained closure",
       value: {
         ...actual,
-        closure: actual.closure.replace("nix copy --no-recursive --option require-sigs true", "nix copy --option require-sigs true"),
+        closure: actual.closure.replace("attic push -j1 --ignore-upstream-cache-filter", "attic push -j1"),
       },
     },

@@ -260,8 +261,8 @@ test("CI boundary checks reject regressions in every asserted direction", async

-          'nix develop .#closurePublisher --command attic push -j1 "pi-daemon-ci:${ATTIC_CACHE}" "$PACKAGE_OUT"',

title: Pin the mode half of path checks, which is a second axis rather than the same policy twice
description:
Reported by pidm-pi-on-demand-dev-test-son after the ownership adoption
(bd-95635b, `630c40b`): the uid half of each path check is now a named policy
with a doc comment and a census, while the mode half is still a raw octal
literal at ~40 sites. Their observation is right that the second half is
unpinned. Their model of it is not, and the difference decides the fix.

The proposed model was that the masks split the same way the root exemption
does — `0o077` for secrets, `0o022` for configuration — so the mask is the same
decision written twice. Correlating every adopted site's ownership policy
against the mask nearest it:

    owner-only    + 0o077        22 sites
    owner-or-root + 0o022         9 sites
    owner-only    + 0o022         9 sites   <- breaks the correlation
    owner-only    + no mask       3 sites
    owner-or-root + both masks    1 site    (dashboard-tls: cert and key differ)

So it holds for 31 of 44 and fails for 9, and those 9 are coherent rather than
accidental: `session-ownership.ts` (3), `session-inventory.ts`, `pi-adapter.ts`
session and root paths (2), `server.ts`, `self-update.ts` bin directory,
`transcript-projector.ts` session source. Each requires the current user to own
the path while tolerating that others may read it. That is a sensible pairing for
session state — only I may have written this, but it need not be unreadable —
and it is not derivable from the ownership policy.

The two axes are therefore independent, and the answer is not to derive the mask
from the policy:

- ownership answers who may have authored the material;
- mode answers who else may read or write it;
- secrets need both strict, provisioned configuration needs a relaxed owner and
  a strict writer, session state needs a strict owner and a relaxed reader.

The 3 no-mask sites are a third kind rather than a gap, and worth keeping
distinct: `server.ts:645` refuses to *replace* a socket it does not own and
`session-inventory.ts:1267,1321` *skip* foreign entries during a scan. They
decide authority to act on a path, not trust in material read from it, so mode
is irrelevant to them. A change that gave every ownership check a mask would be
wrong for these.

Suggested shape, following bd-95635b:

- a policy carrying both axes, chosen per path rather than per module, so
  `owner-only` + "others may read" is expressible and distinct from
  `owner-only` + "others may not";
- the census extended to record both, so a site relaxing its mask is as visible
  as one relaxing its owner;
- the material-trust and authority-to-act shapes kept separate, since only the
  first has a mode at all.

Worth doing for the same reason the ownership half was: a site written with the
wrong mask is currently indistinguishable from one written with the right one,
and no test would notice. Not urgent — nothing here is known to be wrong, and
the correlation analysis above found no site that looks misclassified.

description:

2026-07-29 EXIT CONDITION MET. This tracker's stated condition was "resolve when an upstream Pi release ships protobufjs >=7.6.5". It does.

Verified by the same method this bead's own 2026-07-28 recheck used - npm pack of the published tarball and reading its shrinkwrap, not release notes:
- @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent dist-tags.latest is now 0.82.1
- its published npm-shrinkwrap.json pins node_modules/protobufjs at 7.6.5

title: Allow serve to enable embedded dashboard through explicit CLI overrides
description:
Cacophony's separately supervised Pi Daemon host is headless/Unix-socket-only, while the machine-level instance exposes the useful browser dashboard. Pi Daemon `serve` already accepts API CLI flags, but embedded web enablement/bind/port is currently read only from Pi Daemon YAML; `serve` rejects web CLI options.

Add explicit, typed CLI overrides for embedded web on `pi-daemon serve` so supervisors can configure one self-describing process without generating an extra side config file.

Required surface (names may follow existing config vocabulary):

- `--web-enabled true|false`
- `--web-bind HOST`
- `--web-port PORT`
- optional `--public-origin URL` only if required by the existing embedded dashboard contract
- embedded mode only for `serve`; reject a requested dedicated mode rather than spawning a hidden second process

Semantics/security:

- omitted options preserve current behavior exactly;
- web bind defaults to literal loopback and the first Cacophony canary uses loopback only;
- option-like web values are validated with the same constraints as Pi Daemon's YAML/web command path;
- explicit disable overrides enabling YAML, matching `--api-enabled false` behavior;
- embedded dashboard uses the same resident multiplexer/session catalog and shows logical sessions from this host instance;
- no bearer bytes on argv; API auth remains `--api-token-file`, token fd, env, or generated owner-only `STATE_DIR/api-token` under existing mutual-exclusion rules;
- help, docs and startup/status output identify API and web addresses without exposing token contents;
- clean shutdown covers dashboard server as today.

Acceptance:

1. `serve` with omitted web flags stays socket/API-only according to existing config.
2. `serve --web-enabled true --web-bind 127.0.0.1 --web-port <free>` starts the embedded dashboard and serves the same logical-session inventory as the Unix/API host.
3. Explicit false overrides enabling YAML.
4. Invalid port/bind and incompatible mode combinations fail before publishing listeners.
5. API + web on distinct loopback ports starts and shuts down cleanly; token file stays 0600 and is never logged.
6. Tests prove CLI overrides and YAML precedence without binding public interfaces.
7. A Cacophony consumer can capability-gate the new flags by pinned source revision/version.

This is the upstream half of Cacophony-managed Pi Daemon dashboard observability. The machine-level daemon-main instance on ports 7463/7465 must remain independent.

Implementation checkpoint before broad edits (2026-08-01): precedence will be explicit --web-enabled > YAML web.enabled; explicit --web-bind/--web-port > YAML > existing loopback/default values. Unlike API, --web-port alone will not imply enablement: web exposure stays explicit. Explicit false disables YAML true. serve --web-enabled true rejects YAML mode: dedicated. CLI override validation must complete before Unix/API/web listeners publish. First focused test added before implementation: serve CLI enables embedded Dashboard when YAML omits web; current source is red as expected (1 test, 0 pass, 1 fail; options rejected before lifecycle callback).

title: adapterReadiness reports green from configured credentials, never from a working call
description:
## `adapterReadiness` reports green from CONFIGURED credentials, never from a working call

Observed live on ms-dev (pi-daemon 0.2.2), then traced and confirmed **still present on current main
(0.3.0)**, so this is not fixed by the pending 0.2.2 -> 0.3.0 rollout.

### Live evidence
Host `status` reported, with no session ever opened:
```
adapterReadiness: { ready: true, configuredProviderCount: 5, availableModels: 69,
                    authenticatedModels: 69, authErrorCount: 0, authErrorCodes: [] }
```
Two logical sessions were then opened and driven to a real turn. Every turn failed:
```
stopReason: "error", content: [], usage.totalTokens: 0
errorMessage: Azure OpenAI API error (401): Access denied due to invalid subscription key
              or wrong API endpoint.
```
Readiness stayed `ready: true, authenticatedModels: 69, authErrorCount: 0` throughout.

### Mechanism, on main
`src/pi-adapter.ts:218`
```ts
const authenticatedModels = available.filter((model) =>
  runtime.hasConfiguredAuth(model.provider),
).length;
```
`authenticatedModels` counts models whose provider has credentials **configured**, not credentials
that **work**. The field name asserts a property the computation never checks.

`authErrorCount` / `authErrorCodes` exist and would express exactly this, but `#recordAuthError`
(`src/pi-adapter.ts:186`) is only reachable from startup credential resolution
(`listCredentials()` catch at :173, and the init-error path at :180). No call-time auth failure ever
reaches it, so `authErrorCount` cannot leave 0 once the process has started, and
`ready` (`:222`, `registryError === undefined && authenticatedModels > 0`) cannot go false for bad
credentials.

### Why it matters beyond cosmetics
This readiness field is what an operator and any monitoring path consult to answer "is the host
usable". It answered "yes, 69/69 authenticated" for ~23 hours while the host could not complete a
single turn. In the incident that surfaced this (cacophony:bd-ea3487), that false green is a large
part of why the investigation looked elsewhere: the host advertised full capacity and zero auth
errors while failing every request.

### Suggested shape
Feed call-time auth failures back into the same accounting the struct already has: when a turn fails
with an authentication/authorization error, record the code via the existing `#recordAuthError` path
so `authErrorCount` becomes non-zero and `ready` degrades. That needs no wire change — the fields are
already published.

If instead the intended meaning is "credentials are configured", the field is misnamed and should say
so (`credentialedModels`), so nothing downstream reads it as proof that calls will succeed.

### Not verified by me
I did not attempt the fix. I have no way to exercise a live 401 against a locally built 0.3.0 from
here, and guessing at auth accounting in a codebase I have just met is the same class of error this
bead is about. Evidence and line references above are exact; the design call belongs to this project.

Filed from cacophony:bd-ea3487 (pi-daemon hosting was dead fleet-wide; separate root cause was a
config path defect, now fixed there). Related: bd-99577e, which notes `status` does not report the
model a session is bound to — the same session in this evidence also ignored the `model` supplied at
`open` on 0.2.2 and ran the host default, which is worth checking against 0.3.0 where
`multiplexer.ts:2246/2347` does carry `payload.model` through.

title: [broken-on-main] nix flake check fails: e2e-shell guard rejects the store path it must accept
description:
`nix flake check` fails on main. The `e2e-shell` check throws during evaluation:

```
error: e2e-shell-check: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH carries a store-path reference.
```

Present since ddf077c and invisible until 6dffafe unblocked CI dispatch, so it was red from the moment it landed rather than regressing later.

Cause, and it is a process failure rather than a design one. While verifying the string-context guard I mutated the file to remove `builtins.unsafeDiscardStringContext`, confirmed the guard fired, then "restored" it with `git checkout nix/e2e-shell-check.nix` — which restores from the index, and I had already `git add`ed the mutated version. So the restore was a no-op. The verification that should have caught it ran `nix build ... | tail -1 && echo restored`, where the pipeline's exit status is `tail`'s, so the `&&` fired on a failing build. The commit was then amended from that index. The negative-control mutation shipped as the change.

Two independent mistakes, both of which had to hold: a revert that did not revert, and a check of the wrong exit status.

There is also a real design fault underneath, identified by a reviewer. Composing guard with discard is vacuous: `noContext "..." (unsafeDiscardStringContext x)` can never throw, because the discard guarantees the value has no context. It would have looked protective while asserting nothing — the same vacuity class this session has been about, this time inside the guard written to enforce it.

Fix: the guard applies only to values that should never carry context — `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD`, `PI_DAEMON_PLAYWRIGHT_DRIVER_VERSION`, and the `@playwright/test` pin. `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` is a store path by nature, so it is the documented exception: its context is discarded explicitly, with a comment saying why it is exempt, and its shape is still asserted by `validate` against `/nix/store/*playwright-browsers*`.

6. Return source, focused load evidence, reviewed config rollout, and one canary proving zero queue-full errors.

title: Give the suite a deliberate source of environment variation, and scope what that can and cannot catch
description:
Proposed after four vacuous assertions were found in one night, none by review. Filed as a draft because the design question below is unresolved and worth deciding before anyone builds it.

The observation, from an agent who converged on it independently: every instance was exposed by an environment differing from the authoring one, and none by reading the test. The convention filed as bd-c9c453 tells authors to demonstrate that an assertion can fail, but the mechanism that actually caught these was variation, and the project has no deliberate source of it.

Honest accounting of what a variation lane would have caught, because the case is weaker than it first looks. The four instances:

1. A credential fixture whose permissiveness depended on the runner's umask. Caught by `umask 077`. Cheap and mechanical.
2. A Rich/TUI reading-anchor assertion that compared two pre-hydration values. Needed real CPU contention, so partially reachable by running under load, but the specific window was timing-dependent and would not reproduce reliably.
3. A test pinning an exact npm script string, broken when a preflight was legitimately inserted. Not environmental at all — it took another agent editing the pipeline.
4. Flake source-text assertions that survived an alejandra reformat by luck. Also not environmental — it took a formatter run.

So an environment matrix addresses one and a half of four. That is still worth having, but the framing should be wider than environment: what exposes a vacuous assertion is *departure from the conditions it was written under*, and environment is only one axis. Editing (3) and tooling (4) are the others, and both were supplied here by a second agent doing unrelated work — which is a form of variation the project gets for free from parallelism and cannot rely on when a file has one owner.

Concrete proposal for the mechanical part, deliberately narrow:

- One CI job running the existing Node suite unchanged under a varied environment: `umask 077`, a timezone far from UTC, `LANG=C`, and a constrained `/dev/shm`. Not a new suite and no new assertions — the same tests, different conditions. This is the piece that would have caught (1) outright.
- It should be advisory before it is required. A new axis of variation will surface pre-existing latent assumptions, and turning those into a blocking gate on day one converts a useful signal into pressure to skip tests.

Open questions worth settling first:

- Which axes are worth their runtime, given the project already has three lanes and a macOS job that times out at 25 minutes.
- Whether load-based variation is worth attempting at all, given (2) was found on a shared host by accident and a deliberate loop was argued down earlier tonight on the grounds that the loop changes the load it is measuring.
- Whether the editing and tooling axes can be addressed at all by CI, or whether they are inherently what review and parallel work provide.

Discovered while implementing bd-58a7fa; the convention it follows from is bd-c9c453.

## Folded in from bd-d09b2b, closed as a duplicate of this bead

Two additions from that version, both accepted:

- ~~**Process uid as an axis, alongside umask.**~~ **Withdrawn — see bd-9ad9e5.** Investigated after being proposed, and it argues against itself. The owner-mismatch guards are real and largely untested (41 of them across 21 files, with no test found for the errors they raise), but they are not reachable by a variation lane: running the suite as a different uid does not help, because the fixtures are created by that same uid, so the comparison stays equal. Running as root fails for the same reason. The guard is unreachable by construction in any design where the process that creates the fixture is the process that loads it, which is every lane the project has or could cheaply add. It needs privileged fixture setup, which does not belong in the standard gate, or form 2 from bd-c9c453 — extract the predicate and check in the cases it should reject. Recorded here as a correction rather than removed silently, because "uid is an obvious next axis" is an appealing wrong answer and the reason it fails is not obvious.
- **`PI_DAEMON_PERFORMANCE_BUDGETS` as the precedent for advisory-then-required.** The shape is already in the tree and already accepted: the measurement always runs and prints, and only the assertion is gated behind the switch. A variation lane can do the same — always run and report, gate later — which supplies the advisory phase without inventing a second mechanism.

## Resolved: leave load out

The open question on load-based variation is settled against including it. The reading-anchor instance was found under load-13 contention on a shared host, but what made it diagnosable was instrumenting the pane in a real browser; the load reported that something was wrong without indicating what, and both agents who looked at it spent longer on plausible wrong hypotheses than on the fix. A deliberate load axis would reproduce that experience without reproducing the instrumentation that actually resolved it. Earlier in the same session a load-hunting retry loop was argued down on the related ground that the loop changes the load it is measuring.

That leaves the proposed axes as: umask, timezone, locale, and constrained `/dev/shm`. Uid was considered and withdrawn; see above and bd-9ad9e5.

title: Make a stale dist distinguishable from a real failure in the build-free test loop

The code was correct; a peer had landed that export and the local `dist/` simply
predated it. The message points at a module that looks broken rather than at a
stale build, which is a plausible route to misfiling a broken-on-main bead.

bd-acd227 added `test:src`, which compiles first and is nearly as fast, so the
foot-gun is now avoidable. What is missing is anything that tells you which one
you are in. Options, roughly in order of value:

1. Have `test:unit` compare a cheap fingerprint of `src/**` against one written

2. Failing that, a line in CONTRIBUTING next to `test:unit` naming the hazard
   and pointing at `test:src`.

Deliberately not proposing that `test:unit` build: its whole value is not
building. The gap is that a stale run is indistinguishable from a real failure.

title: The published integration example receives no events: it never attaches
description:
`docs/integration.md` publishes the consumer example Cacophony follows: connect, `client.subscribe(event => ...)` with a `messageUpdate` comment, then `open`, then `wake`. A client doing exactly that receives no events at all.

`docs/protocol.md:81` states the actual rule: "Event delivery is explicit. `open`, `wake`, `status`, `abort`, successful commands, and failed commands never subscribe a connection implicitly. A client must send `attach` with the current `sessionId` and `generation` before it expects events." The behaviour is deliberate and correct; the integration guide simply never mentions `attach`, and its `client.subscribe` line reads as though registering a listener is sufficient.

Measured against a live model rather than inferred, `github-copilot/gemini-3-flash-preview`, two concurrent sessions:

    documented sequence (open, wake)          eventCounts { a: 0, b: 0 }
    with attach between open and wake         eventCounts { a: 14, b: 14 }

`attach` also requires `payload: {}`; omitting it fails validation with `invalid_field: payload`, which the guide would need to show or a reader hits immediately.

The second half is why nobody noticed. `scripts/live-sdk-smoke.mjs` — the only end-to-end check against a real model — records `eventCounts` in its report and never asserts them. It has been printing zeros through every run, including the migration verification earlier tonight, and a zero in a printed report is not a failing test.

So: add `attach` to the integration example with the payload and a sentence on explicit delivery, and make the live smoke assert that events arrive rather than merely counting them. Then a regression in event delivery fails the check that exists to catch it.

title: Prove zero process creation per logical session against a served daemon
description:
`PLAN.md` §"End-to-end consumer" is still open: a Cacophony-facing acceptance that launches the packaged service, creates multiple logical agents, wakes them, and proves no new process appears per wake. It is the property Cacophony deploys this daemon for — one supervised process replacing repeated `pico --resume` / `pi --mode rpc` process creation — and it is currently proven only in-process.

`test/full-host-acceptance.test.mjs` instruments `child_process` inside the test process and forbids spawning, which is strong evidence about the code path but says nothing about the served artefact: the daemon under test is constructed in-process, not started as a process a supervisor would run. A Cacophony deployment gets the latter.

Credential-free slice, which is the half that can land without a live provider:

- start `dist/cli.js serve` as a real child on a temporary socket, state dir, and agent dir, exactly as `test/bootstrap-cli.test.mjs` does;
- connect over the protocol socket and open several logical sessions;
- sample the daemon's descendants from the OS process table before and after, and assert the count is unchanged.

Session creation is the expensive operation Cacophony repeats today, so proving it costs no process is the load-bearing half. The wake half needs either a live provider or a fixture the served daemon can be pointed at, and belongs with the opt-in live SDK path rather than in credential-free CI.

Worth being explicit about what the slice does not prove, so the summary does not overclaim: it establishes zero process creation per logical session through a real process boundary, not per wake, and not through the Nix package. Those are separate follow-ups.

title: Retain a structured browser-suite run record so a local failure classifies itself
description:
A local full browser-suite failure is currently unclassifiable after the fact, because nothing retains the run output. This is not hypothetical: a full-suite run on sonance failed six scenarios in under a second each, and by the time anyone wanted to test what caused it the output was gone, so it could not be distinguished between two candidate mechanisms with different fixes — host starvation, or the browser dying at launch. The latter has a specific signature, `browserContext.newPage: Target page, context or browser has been closed` against every scenario, which is exactly what the CI runner produced in run 30412617437 for bd-df1c84. Five subsequent local runs did not reproduce it.

CI already retains its evidence: the `Dash browser smoke` job uploads `web/test-results` and `web/playwright-report` on failure. A local run has no equivalent, so a one-in-six event is lost rather than recorded.

Proposal, from the agent whose incident this was: add a JSON reporter alongside `list` in `web/playwright.config.ts`, writing to `web/test-results/run.json`. Rationale for the reporter rather than teeing console output — it captures each scenario's error text structurally, which is the property that makes the next occurrence self-classifying, and it avoids ANSI escapes, `pipefail` fragility, and interleaved output. Playwright already writes traces to that directory on failure, so the run record lands beside them, and the directory is already gitignored. Cost on a passing run is effectively zero.

Also add one line to `docs/dash-e2e.md` telling a future investigator to read `web/test-results/run.json` first, and check whether `run.json` should be included in the CI artifact upload for the same reason.

Filed at the request of pidm-pi-on-demand-dev-test-son, who will claim and implement it; their `caco bd create` was returning indeterminately against a flapping helsinki, and under create-only cross-project scope a duplicate could not be seen or closed afterwards. Motivating incident and design are theirs; the observation that the evidence gap is the real defect is from the bd-df1c84 session.

title: Reorder the negative-control forms and record what direct observation costs
description:
The negative-control convention landed in `4910781` (bd-27c44a) lists three
forms in the wrong order, and is missing two constraints found in review.

**Ordering.** It currently reaches for a checked-in negative case first and a
checked precondition second. Review by pidm-pi-on-demand-dev-test-son identified
the flaw: a manual mutation, and to a lesser extent an enumerated negative case,
is exercised in the environment the author is already in. For the umask instance
that is the benign one — deliberately breaking the fail-closed property under a
permissive umask shows the assertion firing correctly, so the ritual passes and
confirms a test that is vacuous elsewhere. A checked precondition fails in
precisely the environment that would otherwise hollow the test out, including
environments nobody on the project has. So it should be first.

Stated narrowly rather than as dominance, because the two forms answer different
questions and neither implies the other: a precondition check proves the setup
still establishes the situation the assertion needs; a negative case proves the
predicate still rejects. The precondition form goes first because it catches
vacuity the author cannot enumerate, not because it subsumes the alternative.

**Missing caveat: what direct observation drags in.** "Assert the effect, not
the spelling" is cheap to state and can be expensive to follow. Interpolating a
store path such as `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` into a check derivation puts that
closure into the check's build inputs — 2.1 GiB of Playwright on every
`nix flake check` in the concrete case. The observation needs its string context
discarded, or the check confined to attributes carrying no store path. Worth
stating, because nobody would guess that observing a value can pull a bundle
into a gate that previously did not need it.

**Missing caveat: lanes.** Direct observation is only free if the lane running
the assertion can perform it. Evaluating a devShell attribute needs Nix, and the
Node gate deliberately has none, so preferring the stronger form can mean moving
an assertion between lanes rather than rewriting it in place.

Scope: reorder and rewrite the CONTRIBUTING section, update
`test/permission-fixture.test.mjs` which asserts the section's shape, and cite
the `playwright-browser-resolution` conversion as the worked example for form 1
once it lands.

title: Run the suite under deliberate environmental variation, starting with umask
description:
Four assertions were found vacuous in one session, in four unrelated areas. The
convention landed tonight (`CONTRIBUTING`, "Negative controls", bd-27c44a /
bd-c9c453 / bd-318c09) tells an author how to demonstrate an assertion can fail.
It does not address how these were actually found, which is worth separating
because the answer is uncomfortable:

- the scroll assertion, by a loaded host (bd-94d7df);
- the umask fixture, by a hardened CI runner (bd-7cba4b);
- the pipeline string, by a legitimate addition to the pipeline (bd-228b91);
- the flake source match, by an alejandra reformat (bd-d79ef1).

None was found by reading the test, and none by review — including the two that
three agents reviewed carefully last night. Every one was found by an environment
differing from the authoring one, and in every case by accident.

So the project relies on environmental variation to find this class, and has no
deliberate source of it. The variation that did the work was incidental: someone
else's runner, host load, an unrelated formatting change.

Cheap deliberate sources, roughly in order of cost:

1. Run the Node suite once under a restrictive umask. That single variation
   would have caught the umask instance directly, and it costs one CI step. It
   is also the variation the project is most exposed to, since none of us has a
   hardened machine and the runners do.
2. Run once with a deliberately hostile `TMPDIR` mode, or as a different uid,
   for the same reason.
3. Consider whether the existing performance-budget switch is the right pattern:
   an opt-in environment that the standard gate does not pay for, but which a
   nightly or on-demand run exercises.

Not proposing mutation testing — too heavy for this codebase and mostly finds

title: An unresolvable model is accepted at open, contrary to the documented refusal
description:
`docs/integration.md` opens with a prerequisite section stating that opening a session "validates that credentials exist for the provider named in `model`, before any turn is attempted", and that a client naming one the instance has no entry for "is refused at `open`, not at `wake`".

Measured, not inferred. Against a freshly served daemon with an isolated state and agent directory:

  payload.model = { provider: "no-such-provider", id: "no-such-model" }
  -> open response ok: true, session created, state idle

So an unresolvable provider/model is accepted at open rather than refused.

`src/pi-adapter.ts:352-370` shows the mechanism. `modelRuntime.getModel(provider, id)` returns undefined for an unknown pair, and `model` then falls back through `scope.scopedModels[0]?.model` to `(await modelRuntime.getAvailable())[0]`. The auth check on the following line tests `model.provider` — the *substituted* model's provider — so it passes. The documented refusal fires only when the named provider resolves to a real model that lacks credentials.

What I verified: the open succeeds. What I did not verify, and what matters more: whether a subsequent wake then runs on the substituted model. `status` does not report the bound model, so confirming it needs a wake and an inspection of which model answered — a credentialed run I did not do rather than a conclusion I am asserting.

If it does substitute, the consequence for Cacophony is direct: it will name a model per agent, and a typo or a model the instance lacks would silently produce a session running on whatever is first available, with no error at open and a plausible answer at wake. That is worse than a refusal in exactly the way tonight's other findings were — the failure is indistinguishable from success from the client's side.

Three possible resolutions, and the choice is a product decision rather than a doc fix:

1. Refuse at open when `model` names a pair the runtime cannot resolve, which is what the guide already promises.
2. Keep the fallback and report the substitution in the open response, so a client can detect it.
3. Keep the behaviour and correct the guide, which currently tells integrators the opposite.

Whichever is chosen, `status` reporting the bound model would make the state observable, which it currently is not.


## Settled: it is silent substitution, measured by pidm-pi-on-demand

The open question above is answered. Opening with `{ provider: "no-such-provider", id: "no-such-model" }`, attaching, and waking with a real turn:

    OPEN ok: true
    WAKE ok: true   (no error)
    EVENTS: 11 | model refs: "provider":"anthropic", "model":"claude-fable-5"

So the turn runs, on a model from a provider the client never named, and nothing in the open response, the wake response, or `status` reports it. The identity was recoverable only by scanning the event stream.

That makes this a product defect rather than a documentation one: the implementation has drifted from the contract the guide states, and the drift is silent in both directions — the client cannot detect the substitution, and the service cannot tell that the client did not mean it.

Raising to P1. A per-agent model typo, or a model a particular instance happens not to carry, yields a working session answering from whatever that instance lists first. For a deployment that assigns models per agent this is a correctness failure that presents as success.

Two coherent resolutions; the choice is product semantics and is with the operator:

1. Refuse at open when `model` names a pair the runtime cannot resolve. This matches the guide's prerequisite section and the neutrality claim that the client provides model policy and the service does not choose one.
2. Substitute deliberately and report the bound model in the open response, so a client can detect and accept it.

Either way `status` should report the bound model, which it currently does not, so the state is observable rather than only inferable from events.

Interim: the guide is being corrected to describe what the implementation does today rather than a refusal that does not happen, without endorsing it as intended behaviour.
