title: Acceptance: launch the packaged daemon as a service and drive the neutral consumer path
description:
PLAN.md section "End-to-end consumer" is unimplemented: "A later Cacophony integration test launches the Nix package as a service, creates multiple logical pico-daemon agents, wakes them, and proves no new process appears per wake."

Current coverage stops short of the artifact. Every protocol and session test runs against `dist/` in the source tree; the built package's only runtime exercise is `installCheckPhase` running `pi-daemon version`, and the home-manager check validates module wiring rather than runtime behaviour. So nothing launches the installed artifact as a service and drives the neutral protocol through it — which is the exact configuration a Cacophony node will deploy.

The wake half needs credentials and stays opt-in. The rest does not, and is worth having in the credential-free gate:

- launch `${package}/bin/pi-daemon serve` against a temporary owner-private state directory
- open several logical sessions over the Unix socket with distinct ids and generations
- exercise the neutral surfaces a consumer uses: subscribe, list, close, and the documented `PiDaemonClient` request shape from docs/integration.md
- assert the process count attributable to the daemon does not grow per session, which is the architectural claim the whole design rests on
- shut down cleanly and assert no orphaned children

Value beyond coverage: it tests the artifact rather than the working tree. The 0.82.1 migration shipped an untracked test helper that every local check passed over and only the Nix package build caught, because the builder sees a source-only tree. A packaged-service acceptance closes the same gap for runtime behaviour rather than for build inputs.

Scope note: this is consumer acceptance, permitted by PLAN.md line 613 as neutral compatibility fixtures and consumer acceptance. It imports nothing from Cacophony and models no bead, message, profile, or token.

title: Say where migration-time verification goes, since it stops meaning anything once the migration lands
description:
While adopting the ownership predicate I wrote a verification script, copied it
into `scripts/`, and then removed it again — which was the right call, but the
reasoning is worth capturing because the pull to keep it was strong.

The script derived each guard's expected policy from `origin/main` and compared
it against the converted source. It was genuinely useful: 44 sites, zero
mismatches, and it failed correctly when a policy was flipped on purpose. But it
compares against `origin/main`, so the moment the conversion lands, `origin/main`
contains the converted code and the comparison becomes vacuous. It would still
run, still pass, and mean nothing — the exact failure mode the convention landed
tonight exists to prevent, in a script rather than a test.

The repository has no convention about this, and the instinct to keep a script
that just did useful work is strong. `scripts/` currently holds seven entries,
all of which are ongoing tooling rather than one-off verification, so the
distinction is being maintained by taste.

Suggested shape, small:

- a line in CONTRIBUTING's testing guidance distinguishing migration-time
  verification from ongoing checks, with the test: if the artifact compares
  against a moving reference such as `origin/main` or a prior revision, its
  result belongs in the commit message and the script does not belong in the
  tree;
- and the corollary that what *does* belong is whatever keeps the migration from
  being undone — in this case an invariant that no module decides ownership
  itself, which keeps meaning something indefinitely.

Not proposing a lint. `scripts/` is small enough that the guidance is the whole
mechanism.

title: Converge flake.nix on its declared alejandra formatter and gate it
description:
`flake.nix` declares `formatter = alejandra`, but the committed file is not alejandra-formatted: running `nix fmt flake.nix` rewrites the entire `pages` derivation block (about 80 lines of indentation churn) that no one intended to touch.

That makes the formatter unusable for a narrow change — a contributor who runs it produces a diff dominated by unrelated reformatting, and one who does not leaves the tree divergent from its own declared formatter. During bd-185516 the reformat had to be reverted and three edits re-applied by hand to keep the diff reviewable.

Fix shape: one deliberate `nix fmt` commit that formats the tree, then a CI check (`nix fmt -- --check`) so it stays converged. The formatting commit should land on its own so it never mixes with behavioural changes.

title: docs/integration.md example fails without credentials for the provider it names
description:
`docs/integration.md` is the document a client integrator follows, and its opening example cannot be run as written without a prerequisite the page never states.

The example names `model: { provider: "github-copilot", id: "gpt-5-mini" }`. Opening a session validates that credentials exist for the named provider before any turn is attempted, so an integrator with no `auth.json` entry for it gets:

```
ProtocolResponseError: failed to open logical session
  cause: PiAdapterError: authentication is not configured for provider: github-copilot
```

Confirmed empirically while writing the consumer acceptance in bd-d54659; the harness had to seed a fixture key for the named provider before the documented request shape would open.

`docs/quickstart.md` does cover `auth.json` as an operator concern, but `integration.md` neither states the prerequisite nor links to it, and the two pages address different readers: quickstart is for someone running the daemon, integration is for someone writing a client against it. The first thing a Cacophony integrator does with this page fails, and the error names a provider rather than a missing setup step.

Fix is a short prerequisite note in `integration.md` stating that opening a session requires credentials for the provider it names, with a link to the quickstart section that establishes them. No code change.

title: [broken-on-main] Dash browser smoke gate fails on the CI runner at browser startup
description:
The `Dash browser smoke` job added in bd-c08a07 fails on the self-hosted CI runner while the identical command passes locally from the same Nix shell.

All three `@smoke` scenarios fail at browser startup, not on any assertion. From the uploaded `dash-smoke-playwright` artifact for run 30412617437 (commit 0692906), every error-context.md reports:

    Error: browserContext.newPage: Target page, context or browser has been closed

The preceding step, `nix develop .#e2e --command npm ci --ignore-scripts`, succeeded, and the browser-revision preflight is inside the failing script, so the bundle itself resolved. Locally `just dash-e2e-smoke` passes in 48-53s on the same commit and the same nixpkgs Playwright driver.

Leading hypothesis: the runner executes as root or in a container without user namespaces, so Chromium's sandbox aborts at launch. That is the standard cause of this exact message on self-hosted Linux runners, and it explains why a normal-user local run is unaffected. A `/dev/shm` size limit is the other common cause with the same signature.

Do not simply disable the sandbox globally. Preferred order:
1. Read the completed job log for Chromium's own stderr, which usually names the cause outright ("Running as root without --no-sandbox is not supported").
2. If it is the sandbox, gate the relaxation behind an explicit CI-only environment variable consumed by playwright.config.ts launch options, documented in docs/dash-e2e.md, so a developer machine never silently runs an unsandboxed browser.
3. If it is /dev/shm, prefer raising the runner's shared memory over disabling the sandbox.

Until this is fixed the smoke gate is red on main for reasons unrelated to any change under review, which is precisely the failure mode the bd-c08a07 assessment argued against. Priority is therefore P1: a permanently red gate is worse than no gate.

Note main also shows pre-existing failures on Node 22.19.0, Node 24, and Nix (macOS) from at least d93900d, which are separate from this and predate the smoke job.

title: Make source-text assertions tolerate layout so formatting cannot turn main red
description:
A formatting-only Nix change turned `main` red because `test/release.test.mjs`
asserts the exact source text of `flake.nix`:

    assert.match(flake, /pages = pkgs\.runCommand "pi-daemon-pages"/);

Alejandra wraps that onto two lines, so a change with no semantic effect broke a
test. Fixed in bd-d79ef1 by matching the semantic fact instead of the layout,
but the pattern is broader than this one line.

Several tests assert repository source text with regexes: `release.test.mjs`
over `flake.nix` and workflow files, `chat-pane-layout.test.ts` over component
sources, `npm-deps-hash.test.mjs` and `nix-format.test.mjs` over `flake.nix`,
`Justfile`, and CI yaml. These are genuinely useful — they are how the repository
gates wiring and structure that has no runtime surface — but each one silently
couples a formatter, a linter, or a reviewer's whitespace preference to a
passing suite.

Suggested shape, in rough order of value:

1. A short convention note in CONTRIBUTING: when asserting source text, assert
   the semantic fact and tolerate layout. Prefer parsing over regex where a
   parser already exists, for example `JSON.parse` for `package.json` rather
   than a regex over its text; several tests already do this and are the model.
2. Where layout tolerance is impractical, make the assertion name the coupling
   in a comment so the next formatter change has a pointer.

Not proposing removing the assertions. The gap is that nothing tells an author
the coupling exists until CI goes red.

title: [operator-action] Restore sonance Pi Daemon after zero-disk outage
description:
Caco-owned Pi Daemon is desired Running but actual stopped on sonance. This is not a Pi Daemon code fault; the host has hard disk exhaustion and a stale PID.

READ-ONLY EVIDENCE 2026-08-01:
- `caco @sonance sidecar status --service pi-daemon`: desired=Running actual=stopped (pid-only)
- `caco @sonance node status --node sonance`: caco-daemon running, pi-daemon stopped
- `caco @sonance doctor --local-only`: overall unhealthy; free disk 0.00 GiB of 224.5 GB (0%); queue-admission watermark requires 25 GiB; pi-daemon pid-only owner=stale_pid pid=2303586; action hint is `caco up` only after cleanup
- `caco @sonance log exceptions ...` cannot commit to the daemon store: sqlite database or disk is full
- `caco @sonance node disk`: Caco-owned categories total 16.7 GiB, dominated by daemon_checkouts 10.6 GiB, but doctor says the dominant whole-host filler is stale reint-gate-target dirs (20-32 GiB each); node-disk categories are not a full df replacement
- no Pi Daemon service log lines exist

title: Prove the packaged binary serves without creating a process
description:
Extends bd-c4c80b from the code to the artefact. That acceptance runs `dist/cli.js`; a Cacophony deployment installs the Nix package and its Home Manager service runs `.../bin/pi-daemon serve`. `nix/home-manager-module-check.nix` proves the generated service *configuration* is right and never launches it, so nothing had established that the packaged binary serves at all.

Opt-in, because building the package runs the full suite in `checkPhase` and takes minutes, which the deterministic gate must not depend on. It builds nothing itself: point `PI_DAEMON_PACKAGE_ROOT` at an existing `nix build .#pi-daemon` result so the acceptance measures the artefact rather than the build.

Two environment assumptions surfaced while writing it, both of which failed only outside the developer machine and are worth recording because they are the same class:

1. The process-table walk shelled out to `ps`, which the Nix build sandbox does not provide — `spawn ps ENOENT`, exactly the shape of the `openssl` dependency that broke the Node CI lane. Fixed by reading `/proc` where it exists and keeping `ps` only as the macOS fallback, which removes the dependency rather than declaring it.
2. The auth fixture named a provider literally. That matched by accident locally and failed in the sandbox with "no authenticated Pi model is available". It now derives the provider from the SDK's own model registry, so the fixture cannot drift from what the SDK actually knows.

Verified end to end: `nix build .#pi-daemon` succeeds with the new test in the sandbox, and the packaged binary serves two logical sessions and gains no descendant process.

title: [broken-on-main] Browser smoke gate still fails at launch; capture the browser's own stderr
description:
Follow-up to bd-df1c84, which was the wrong fix. The `Dash browser smoke` job still fails on the self-hosted runners with all three scenarios reporting

    Error: browserContext.newPage: Target page, context or browser has been closed

on run 30419966285 (commit 419c750), which already contains the sandbox relaxation landed at 7843343.

What is now ruled out:

- Environment passthrough. `PI_DAEMON_E2E_NO_SANDBOX` does reach the config through `nix develop .#e2e --command`, verified directly: `PI_DAEMON_E2E_NO_SANDBOX=1 nix develop .#e2e --command node -e '...'` prints `"1"`. So `--no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage` were applied and the browser still died at launch.
- The browser bundle itself. The revision preflight passes in the job, and the same bundle runs the suite locally.

So neither the Chromium sandbox nor `/dev/shm` sizing explains it, and the cause is still unknown. Note the runners vary between runs: `pi-daemon-ms-dev-4` for run 30412617437 and `pi-daemon-ms-dev-3` for 30419966285, so this is not one bad host.

The blocker is diagnostic, not analytical: Playwright swallows the browser's own stderr unless `DEBUG=pw:browser` is set, so every failure so far reports the symptom and none report the cause. Guessing again would be a third round trip on a gate that is already red.

Proposal: add a `web/scripts/check-browser-launch.mjs` preflight that launches Chromium with the same launch options the suite uses, and on failure prints the browser's own stderr and exit status rather than Playwright's generic message. Run it alongside the existing revision preflight in `e2e:nix` and `e2e:smoke`. Two benefits beyond this incident: the job fails in seconds with a self-describing message instead of three identical scenario failures two minutes in, and a contributor whose machine cannot launch the browser gets told why.

Then read the next run's log and fix the actual cause.

Note the smoke job is not the only red on main: bd-7cba4b (openssl on the Node lane) is still open and unowned, so main CI is red regardless of this bead.

title: Protocol v2: host scoped neutral tool adapters without arbitrary extensions
description:
Cacophony child bd-2d5c3c cannot enable project-bound pico-daemon tools against current pi-daemon protocol v1: ResourcePolicy.tools is the literal type "none", validateResources rejects every non-none value as unsupported_resource_policy, and SessionAdapter has no capability transport. Add a general-purpose host-side scoped neutral tool-adapter contract without importing Cacophony concepts. Requirements: versioned descriptor passed at open (owner-local Unix endpoint plus opaque session-bound capability handle, never bearer/PKI/env); fixed allowlisted neutral operations rather than arbitrary extension loading or shell; per-session generation binding; root-confined filesystem semantics; request/idempotency/size/concurrency/time bounds; adapter identity and response validation; no inherited ambient environment; close/restart revocation; cross-session and confused-deputy adversarial tests. Keep protocol v1 no-tools behavior unchanged and default-off. Cacophony will supply the project-bound adapter endpoint/token in bd-2d5c3c after this host contract lands.

---

title: Dash auth enforcement: identity-bound HTTP, stream and no-leak policy
description:
Child slice of bd-b31a5d. After bd-07a348, wire identity-bound browser sessions and the central policy ledger through every Dashboard HTTP and WebSocket boundary in embedded and dedicated modes. Filter inventory with bounded opaque per-principal paging; enforce read/control/admin for info, transcript, activation, tickets, drafts, schedules, export and Rich/TUI channels; preserve daemon service-bearer isolation; and return indistinguishable not-found responses for absent versus unauthorized resources. Retain the exact single-local-owner compatibility migration and do not expose multi-user mode until enforcement is complete.

Implemented in 451b0e5 on current main base: one DashboardAuthorizationEnforcer wraps every HTTP and official Rich/TUI browser boundary in embedded and dedicated modes; principal/query-bound bounded scan-ahead cursors expose continuations only for known authorized records; absent/unauthorized direct lookups share content-free not_found; workspaces are identity-derived in multi-user mode; drafts/tickets/exports/schedules register owner policies; stream frames/events revalidate provider and policy with bounded event queues and release channels on revocation; settings mutation/scheduler aggregates are administrator-only; remote backends retain machine bearer isolation. Multi-user config remains unavailable. Post-rebase focused enforcement/backend/server/CLI suite 72/72, clean package/release 11/11, and Pages derivation passed.

title: Dash session ownership: direct co-opt, safe fork/import, conflict detection and export
description: Implement SessionOwnershipService and session storage policy. Permit only the canonical Pi sessions subdirectory as a narrow data root while keeping auth/config siblings forbidden. New Dash sessions default configurably to normal Pi session storage. Existing sessions support reuse, explicit direct/co-opt with user warning, or fork/import with new UUID. Add owner/symlink/root/cwd checks, source fingerprints, durable idempotent ownership tickets/mappings, cooperative leases, daemon/controller checks, best-effort open-writer observation, pre-write prefix/mtime/inode validation, external_write_conflict fail-closed behavior, and fork recovery. Add export-as-new to stock Pi, guarded unchanged-prefix append-back, export-and-release, atomic owner-private publication, and immediate inventory updates. Never silently overwrite divergent source or create two daemon writers.

title: Implement bounded host tool-adapter runtime registry and per-session Pi injection
description: Complementary implementation child of bd-fc8275; contract/schema sibling is bd-5c06cd. Build the product-neutral runtime seam that consumes an already validated HostToolAdapterDescriptor and exposes only the fixed filesystem-neutral operations (`fs.list`, `fs.stat`, `fs.read`, `fs.search`, `fs.write`, `fs.edit`) as Pi custom tools. Own a focused adapter client/registry module plus PiSessionFactory injection and unit tests. Enforce owner-local private Unix socket checks, cwd-root-relative path normalization with symlink/traversal fail-closed behavior, session/generation/host-instance identity on every request and response, bounded NDJSON request/response size, concurrency/queue/time limits, idempotency metadata, adapter identity/version validation, abort propagation, and disposal/revoke on close or session replacement. Never load an extension, expose shell/process/network/remove, inherit ambient environment, or spawn a child process. Protocol v1 and every open with `tools:"none"` must remain exactly no-tools/default-off. Treat the capability handle as secret: no logs, errors, status, details, event payloads, or persistence. Coordinate the exact exported descriptor and operation request shapes with bd-5c06cd owner before editing shared runtime-facing types. Keep protocol/schema/docs, multiplexer/server persistence wiring, root end-to-end conformance, web/dashboard, and scheduler files out of this slice; root owner aurora-pi-daemon-pidm-dev-aur-2 will integrate those.
